page_data.en:
Memorandum on V.A. Chilikin, editor of the
"Novosti Dnia" (Russian Daily News).

Vassily Alexandrovich CHILIKIN, Russian,
was born on 29-10-1892 in Riasan Province,
Russia. Prior to 1918 he is reported to have
been working as a journalist in Moscow after
which he proceeded to Vladivostok where he was
engaged in commercial pursuits for some time.
In 1921 he went to Harbin where he resumed his
journalistic activities. He first published a
weekly Russian newspaper entitled "Commercial
Telegraph" and in 1923 started the publication
of a daily newspaper "Kopeika". During the
three years of the publication of the latter
newspaper its political colour changed from
"White" to pro-Soviet and vice-versa to suit
the conveniences of the editor and, consequently,
Chilikin acquired the reputation of being a
political opportunist. In 1926 the "Kopeika"
is reported to have been closed by order of the
local Chinese Authorities for publishing certain
offensive articles.

In September, 1926 Chilikin came to
Shanghai and soon afterwards started a printing
establishment known as the "Asia Press". In
December, 1927 he started the publication of a
Russian daily newspaper entitled "Utre" in the
French Concession, which he later sold to the
late Mr. Lembich, owner of the "Shanghai Zaria",
in July, 1928. The newspaper was renamed "Rebe"
and until the end of 1928 Chilikin continued to
be its editor. In April, 1929 he left for Harbin.
page_data.zh:
关于《今日新闻》（Russian Daily News）编辑 V.A. 奇利金（Chilikin）的备忘录。

瓦西里·亚历山德罗维奇·奇利金（Vassily Alexandrovich CHILIKIN），俄罗斯人，1892年10月29日出生于俄罗斯梁赞省（Riasan Province）。据报道，1918年之前他在莫斯科从事记者工作，随后前往海参崴，在那里从事了一段时间的商业活动。1921年他前往哈尔滨，恢复了记者活动。他首先出版了一份名为《商业电报》（Commercial Telegraph）的俄文周报，并于1923年开始出版日报《戈比》（Kopeika）。在该报出版的三年间，其政治色彩从“白俄”转变为亲苏，反之亦然，以迎合编辑的需要，因此，奇利金获得了政治投机分子的名声。据报道，1926年，《戈比》因刊登某些冒犯性文章而被当地中国当局下令关闭。

1926年9月，奇利金来到上海，不久后创办了一家名为“亚细亚印刷所”（Asia Press）的印刷机构。1927年12月，他在法租界开始出版一份名为《早晨》（Utre）的俄文日报，后来于1928年7月将其出售给已故的伦比奇（Lembich）先生，后者是《上海霞光报》（Shanghai Zaria）的所有者。该报更名为《雷贝》（Rebe），直到1928年底，奇利金一直担任其编辑。1929年4月，他前往哈尔滨。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

During his early journalistic activities
in Shanghai Chilikin was assaulted in 1927 by
two Russians who objected to an article which
appeared in the "Utro". In January, 1928 an
unsuccessful private criminal prosecution was
brought against him in the former French Mixed
Court by the local agency of the Chinese Eastern
Railway, a Soviet concern, in connection with a
series of articles he published regarding the
"criminal activities of Bolsheviks in Shanghai".

In April, 1930 Chilikin returned to
Shanghai from Harbin and during the same year
opened a printing establishment in the French
Concession known as the "Standard Press". About
the same time his wife established the library
and bookstore "Skify" at 645 Avenue Joffre which
was later removed to 289 Avenue du Roi Albert.
The latter enterprise has ceased to exist.

In March, 1935 Chilikin applied to the
local French Authorities for permission to
publish a Russian daily newspaper "Kopeika" -
a "non-political organ the main purpose of which
was to furnish news to the poorer classes of the
Russian community who could not afford buying
larger and more expensive newspapers". The
French Police report regarding this application
was unfavourable to Chilikin and described him
as an unprincipled individual, political opportunist
and suspected Soviet agent. On the other hand,
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

在上海早期的记者活动中，奇利金于1927年遭到两名俄罗斯人的袭击，他们反对《早晨》（Utro）上刊登的一篇文章。1928年1月，中东铁路（一家苏联企业）的本地代理机构就他发表的一系列关于“布尔什维克在上海的犯罪活动”的文章，在前法公廨对他提起私人刑事诉讼，但未获成功。

1930年4月，奇利金从哈尔滨返回上海，并于同年年在法租界开设了一家名为“标准印刷所”（Standard Press）的印刷机构。大约在同一时间，他的妻子在霞飞路645号建立了“斯基泰”（Skify）图书馆和书店，后来迁至阿尔伯特国王路289号。后者已不复存在。

1935年3月，奇利金向当地法国当局申请许可，出版一份名为《戈比》（Kopeika）的俄文日报——这是一个“非政治性刊物，主要目的是为那些买不起更大、更昂贵报纸的俄罗斯社区贫困阶层提供新闻”。法国警方关于此申请的报告对奇利金不利，将他描述为一个无原则的人、政治投机分子和疑似苏联代理人。另一方面，

page_data.en:
- 3 -

however, he was recommended by a prominent
French resident as an honest man, full of energy,
whose newspaper might eventually become an
instrument of propaganda in the hands of the
French Authorities. The necessary permission
was granted.

In October, 1934 the newspaper was renamed
the "Novosti Dnia" and its editorial and printing
offices were removed from 11 Route de Sieyes to
785 Avenue Joffre. At this time its financial
position was described by the French Police as
very precarious. However, towards the end of
1934 it became evident that Chilikin had obtained
certain funds from an unknown source. During
the ensuing two years the "Novosti Dnia" gradually
increased the number of its pages and in 1937
appeared in a 12 page edition.

The political physiognomy of this newspaper
as well/its attitude towards various practical
problems with which the local Russian community
is faced have been difficult to define. On
May 26, 1936 an editorial entitled "JUSTIFIED
PRIDE" appeared in the "Novosti Dnia" in which
general principles were outlined of the policy
this newspaper claims to have been following
for the previous three years. According to
this editorial, the "Novosti Dnia" was an
"absolutely independent non-party organ" of
Russian emigres and pursued only one aim, namely:
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

然而，一位著名的法国居民推荐他是一个诚实、充满活力的人，他的报纸最终可能成为法国当局手中的宣传工具。必要的许可被授予。

1934年10月，该报更名为《今日新闻》（Novosti Dnia），其编辑部和印刷厂从赛义斯路11号迁至霞飞路785号。当时，法国警方形容其财务状况非常岌岌可危。然而，到了1934年底，很明显奇利金已从不明来源获得了一定资金。在接下来的两年里，《今日新闻》逐渐增加了页数，并在1937年以12页版发行。

这份报纸的政治面貌以及它对当地俄罗斯社区面临的各种实际问题的态度一直难以界定。1936年5月26日，《今日新闻》刊登了一篇题为《合理的自豪》的社论，其中概述了该报声称在过去三年中一直遵循的政策的一般原则。根据这篇社论，《今日新闻》是俄罗斯移民的“绝对独立的无党派机关”，只追求一个目标，即：

page_data.en:
- 4 -

"to facilitate by every means an improvement
of the economic and cultural standard of living
of the Russian community and to struggle against
any oppressors of the Russian people".

References made in the editorial in
question regarding the various "enemies" of the
"Novosti Dnia" show that Mr. Chilikin's efforts
in the direction indicated were far from being
generally appreciated among the Russian community.
Indeed, it is evident to every regular reader of
the local Russian press that for reasons which
are not always clear, Mr. Chilikin has been at
war with all other Russian newspapers published
in Shanghai, with the exception of Soviet
newspapers, such as the now defunct "China Daily
Herald", "Na Rodinu" and "New Life", which have
been immune from his attacks. It is not known
what Mr. Chilikin's ideas were as to how his
professed aims were to be realised and hardly
anything constructive has ever been suggested by
him. On the other hand his vicious attacks on
the "National Committee of Russian Emigrants'
Association" and the "Russian Emigrants' Committee"
are well known, as well as the fact that these
two bodies, whatever their weaknesses might have
been, represented practically all Russian
organisations engaged in genuine work on behalf
of their nationals.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

“尽一切手段促进俄国侨民经济和文化生活水平的提高，并与任何压迫俄国人民的人作斗争”。

上述社论中提及《今日新闻》（Novosti Dnia）的各种“敌人”，表明奇利金先生（Mr. Chilikin）在上述方向上的努力并未在俄国侨民中得到普遍认可。事实上，当地俄文报刊的每一位常规读者都清楚，出于并不总是明确的原因，奇利金先生一直与上海出版的所有其他俄文报纸处于交战状态，唯独苏联报纸除外，如现已停刊的《中国每日先驱报》（China Daily Herald）、《归乡》（Na Rodinu）和《新生活》（New Life），这些报纸未受其攻击。人们不知道奇利金先生对于如何实现其宣称的目标有何想法，他也几乎从未提出过任何建设性建议。另一方面，他对“俄国侨民协会全国委员会”（National Committee of Russian Emigrants' Association）和“俄国侨民委员会”（Russian Emigrants' Committee）的恶毒攻击众所周知，尽管这两个机构可能存在种种弱点，但它们实际上代表了所有真正为本国同胞开展工作的俄国组织。

page_data.en:
- 5 -

The scandalous campaigns conducted by
the "Novosti Dnia" from time to time in connection
with various matters relating to the inner life
of the Russian community invariably created an
atmosphere of ill-feeling and animosity on account
of the reckless, irresponsible and invariably
vulgar manner they were carried out and are known
to have aroused strong resentment and indignation
in the community.

Mr. Chilikin's activities were often
unfavourably commented upon in the local Russian
press and on one occasion were publicly censured
by the "National Committee" referred to above.
However, this worried Mr. Chilikin very little
and he continued his practice of singling out
this or that individual or organisation as the
target of his ridicule which very often went
beyond the limits of common decency.

Suspicions have been quite openly expressed
in certain circles of the local Russian community
that in his activities Mr. Chilikin was guided
and supported by a third party pursuing aims
which have nothing to do with the welfare of the
Russian community. The open pro-Soviet attitude
of the "Novesti Dnia" since the latter part of
1936 bears out these suspicions. Anonymous
leaflets which appeared in Shanghai from time to
time went still farther in this direction and
branded the editor of the "Novesti Dnia" as a
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

《今日新闻》不时就涉及俄国侨民内部生活的各种事项进行的丑闻式宣传，因其鲁莽、不负责任且一贯低俗的方式， invariably 造成了不和与敌意的氛围，并已知在社区中引起了强烈的怨恨和愤慨。

当地俄文报刊经常对奇利金先生的活动给予不利评论，有一次还受到上述“全国委员会”的公开谴责。然而，这并未让奇利金先生感到多少困扰，他继续将个人或组织 singled out 作为其嘲笑的目标，这种嘲笑往往超出了基本礼节的界限。

当地俄国侨民的某些圈子相当公开地表示怀疑，认为奇利金先生的活动受到第三方的指导和支持，而该第三方追求的目标与俄国侨民的福祉无关。自1936年下半年以来，《今日新闻》公开的亲苏态度证实了这些怀疑。不时在上海出现的匿名传单在这方面走得更远，给《今日新闻》的主编贴上了

page_data.en:
2
- 6 -

Soviet agent-provocateur. Whatever truth may
be in these accusations, there is little doubt
that the "Novosti Dnia" displayed many features
characteristic of the "yellow press".

For the purpose of a summing-up the
following characteristic of V.A. Chilikin may
be quoted which, although given by the now defunct
local Russian magazine "Parus" - Chilikin's
arch-enemy -, nevertheless contains a great deal
of truth :-

"Vassily Chilikin, commonly known under
the contemptuous name "Vaska Chilikin", is a
man devoid of any principles. It is not known
that he ever had any principles. Nothing is
sacred to him: neither Motherland, nor his own
people, nor church, nor God. But he has his
POCKET - his holy of holies - and CYNICISM
and IMPUDENCE. Nothing can disconcert him or
make him feel ashamed. Generally speaking, he
does not know what shame is: he was beaten up,
insults of all sorts were hurled at him, but he
is utterly indifferent to all this and keeps on
following his own path, along which dollars can
be found. Dollars, only dollars - this is what
he wants. For dollars he is ready to sell
everything - honour, Motherland and God. Such
a person is publishing a daily newspaper through
the medium of which he can attack various
page_data.zh:
2
- 6 -

苏联挑衅特工（agent-provocateur）的标签。无论这些指控有多少真实性，毫无疑问，《今日新闻》表现出许多“黄色新闻”的特征。

为了总结起见，可以引用以下关于 V.A. 奇利金的特征描述，虽然这是由现已停刊的当地俄文杂志《帆船》（Parus）——奇利金的死敌——提供的，但仍包含大量事实：

“瓦西里·奇利金，通常被轻蔑地称为‘瓦斯卡·奇利金’（Vaska Chilikin），是一个毫无原则的人。据知他从未有过任何原则。对他来说没有什么是神圣的：既无祖国，也无同胞，既无教会，也无上帝。但他有他的‘口袋’——他的至圣所——以及‘犬儒主义’和‘厚颜无耻’。没有什么能让他慌乱或感到羞愧。一般来说，他不知羞耻为何物：他挨过打，遭受过各种侮辱，但他对此完全漠不关心，继续沿着自己的道路前行，在这条路上可以找到美元。美元，只有美元——这就是他想要的。为了美元，他准备出卖一切——荣誉、祖国和上帝。就是这样一个人，通过出版一份日报，借此攻击各种

page_data.en:
- 7 -

individuals and institutions, bring dissension
and disorganization into the Russian community.
And he dares call his newspaper an emigrant and
nationalist newspaper!" .....

Being a past master in the art of
"mudslinging" Chilikin was bound to come to the
notice of the police authorities of both the
French Concession and the International Settlement.
In August, 1935, acting on an impulse that the
French Police Authorities were obstructing him
and his publication, Chilikin removed the
editorial and printing offices of the "Novosti
Dnia" from the French Concession to 620 Avenue Foch
in the Settlement. According to the French
Police, this was the result of a warning given to
Chilikin in connection with several complaints
regarding his blackmailing activities.

In September, 1935 an order for the ban
on the sale of the "Novosti Dnia" was issued by
the French Authorities, the reason for the ban
being articles published in that newspaper which
contained sarcastic criticism of the policy of
the French Municipal Council, The ban was lifted
only after the "Novosti Dnia" had published a
full apology for the article in question.

In December, 1936 D. G.(Special Branch)
was obliged to draw Mr. Chilikin's attention to
the danger of the promises he was giving in
his newspaper at that time to a controversy over
page_data.zh:
- 7 -

个人和机构，在俄国侨民中制造分裂和无序。而他竟敢称他的报纸为侨民和民族主义报纸！”……

作为一名“抹黑”艺术的大师，奇利金必然引起法租界和公共租界警察当局的注意。1935年8月，出于一种冲动，认为法国警察当局正在阻碍他及其出版物，奇利金将《今日新闻》的编辑部和印刷厂从法租界迁至租界内的福煦路620号。据法国警方称，这是由于针对其勒索活动的几起投诉而向奇利金发出警告的结果。

1935年9月，法国当局发布禁令，禁止销售《今日新闻》，禁令原因是该报刊登的文章包含对法国公董局政策的讽刺性批评。只有在《今日新闻》就有关文章发表完整道歉后，禁令才被解除。

1936年12月，特别处（D. G.）不得不提请奇利金先生注意，他在当时的报纸中就犹太问题争议所作的承诺存在危险，并要求他不再提及该主题。

page_data.en:
- 8 -

the Jewish question and requested him to refrain
from further reference to the subject.

In January, 1936 upon receipt of a complaint
from Mr. Ch. E. Metzler, Chairman of the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, regarding Chilikin's
demagogic campaign against Russian public and
benevolent organizations D. C. (Special Branch)
again called Mr. Chilikin to his office and
requested him to be less vitriolic in his
pronouncements and to avoid publishing articles
savouring exaggeration.

On 25-10-36, 8-1-37 and 13-1-37 in
connection with articles of the "Novosti Dnia"
insulting to the German people, the D. C. (Special
Branch) warned the editor of the newspaper to
refrain from publishing anything likely to offend
religious or national feelings of any section
of the foreign community in Shanghai.

On March 25, 1937 a complaint was received
from Mr. J.A. Thompson regarding the "dastardly
manner" in which the "Novosti Dnia" had reported
the inquest proceeding in H.B.M. Consular Court
on the body of his late daughter. Complainant
stated that the report was "evidently calculated
to pander to the scandal-mongering section of
the Russian community" and was injurious to his
late daughter's good name. Called up to Headquarters
in this connection Mr. Chilikin tendered his
apologies to Mr. Thompson.
page_data.zh:
- 8 -

1936年1月，收到俄国侨民委员会主席 Ch. E. Metzler 先生关于奇利金针对俄国公共和慈善组织开展煽动性运动的投诉后，特别处（D. C.）再次将奇利金先生召至办公室，要求他在言论中少些尖刻，避免刊登带有夸张色彩的文章。

1936年10月25日、1937年1月8日和1937年1月13日，鉴于《今日新闻》刊登侮辱德国人民的文章，特别处（D. C.）警告该报编辑，不要刊登任何可能冒犯上海外侨社区任何部分宗教或民族感情的内容。

1937年3月25日，收到 J.A. Thompson 先生的投诉，称《今日新闻》以“卑鄙的方式”报道了其已故女儿在英国驻华领事法庭的死因调查程序。投诉人指出，该报道“显然是为了迎合俄国侨民中喜欢散布丑闻的那部分人”，并有损其已故女儿的名誉。为此事被召至总部时，奇利金先生向汤普森先生表示了歉意。

page_data.en:
- 9 -

Since the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in North-China the "Novosti Dnia"
has adopted a pro-Chinese attitude (vide attached
translation of his letter to M-me Sun Yat-sen).
While there are many Russians in Shanghai who
sympathise with China in her present struggle,
Chilikin's manner of supporting China aroused
alarm and protests among the Russian community.
During August, 1937 a complaint was received by
the Municipal Police and two by the Secretary
of the Municipal Council regarding articles
published in the "Novosti Dnia" containing
malicious insinuations directed against certain
individuals and institutions in connection with
their alleged pro-Japanese attitude. All
complaints drew the attention of the authorities
to the fact that Chilikin's libellous statements
were tantamount to inciting the Chinese against
the Russian population in Shanghai. As a result,
the publication of the "Novosti Dnia" was
suspended by the Municipal Police on 8-9-37
under Emergency Orders.

Chilikin at first made no attempt to
conceal his anti-Police sentiments during the
course of every day conversation and it was not
until he realised the futility of endeavouring
to obtain "protection" elsewhere for his newspaper
against the "persecutions" of the Municipal Police
that he deemed it advisable to appeal to the
Shanghai Municipal Council expressing his regrets
page_data.zh:
- 9 -

自华北中日敌对行动爆发以来，《今日新闻》采取了亲华态度（参见附译其致孙逸仙夫人的信件）。虽然上海有许多俄国人在中国目前的斗争中同情中国，但奇利金支持中国的方式在俄国侨民中引起了恐慌和抗议。1937年8月期间，工部局警务处收到一起投诉，工部局秘书收到两起投诉，均涉及《今日新闻》刊登的文章，这些文章包含针对某些个人和机构的恶意暗示，指控他们持亲日态度。所有投诉都提请当局注意，奇利金的诽谤性言论等同于煽动中国人反对上海的俄国居民。结果，工部局警务处于1937年9月8日根据紧急命令暂停了《今日新闻》的出版。

起初，奇利金在日常交谈中毫不掩饰其反警察情绪，直到他意识到试图为其报纸寻求其他地方“保护”以对抗工部局警务处的“迫害”是徒劳的之后，他才认为向上海工部局申诉、表达悔意并请求允许恢复出版该报是明智之举。在奇利金书面承诺 1) 停止攻击本社区的白俄，以及 2) 不再刊登任何形式的令人反感或辱骂性内容后，这一请求于1937年9月27日获得批准。

page_data.en:
- 10 -

and asking for permission to resume the publication
of the paper. This was granted on 27-9-37 after
Chilikin had given written undertaking to 1) cease
his attacks on the White Russians in this community
and 2) refrain from publishing objectionable or
abusive matter of any kind.

On 20-12-37 and on 5-5-39 he was informed
by the Municipal Police that his paper had come
to the notice of the Japanese authorities in
connection with the important part it seemed to
take in anti-Japanese activities and was warned
to refrain from publishing anything that might
offend the susceptibilities of Japanese nationals.

On 2-3-39 he was warned that the Police
strongly objected to the generally insulting
character of verses accompanying various anti-
German Nazi cartoons which appeared in his paper
in February, 1939 and that this attitude was
not in keeping with his written undertaking of
September, 1937.

On 25-1-40 he was ordered by the Police
to discontinue further reference to a certain
case of which he took advantage for the launching
of a campaign against the Russian Emigrants
Committee etc. in his usual malicious and abusive
style.

In a letter dated June 30, 1939 Chilikin
informed the Municipal Police that he ceased to
page_data.zh:
- 10 -

1937年12月20日和1939年5月5日，工部局警务处通知他，由于其报纸似乎在反日活动中扮演重要角色，已引起日本当局的注意，并警告他不要刊登任何可能冒犯日本国民感情的内容。

1939年3月2日，警方警告他，强烈反对他在1939年2月的报纸上刊登的各种反德国纳粹漫画所配诗句的普遍侮辱性质，并指出这种态度不符合他1937年9月的书面承诺。

1940年1月25日，警方命令他停止进一步提及某一案件，他正利用该案件以其惯用的恶毒和辱骂风格发起针对俄国侨民委员会等的运动。

在1939年6月30日的一封信中，奇利金通知工部局警务处，他自1939年6月19日起不再是无国籍人士，因为他已向苏联政府申请公民身份，并从苏联总领事馆获得了“注册证书”。

page_data.en:
- 11 -

be a person without nationality as from 19-6-39,
having applied to the Government of the U.S.S.R.
for citizenship and obtained from the Soviet
Consulate General a certificate of registration".

Following the outbreak of the present
war in Europe the "Novosti Dnia" sharply changed
its attitude towards Germany and was the only
Russian newspaper in Shanghai, which gave prominence
to the news carried by the Transocean Agency.
However, recently a distinct change in favour of
France and Great Britain has been evident.

It may be taken for granted that among
other things, Chilikin is a person non grata
with the Japanese and that he is fully aware of this.
Hence the gradual fading away of the anti-Japanese
attitude of the "Novosti Dnia" during the past
several months. This seems to be a very wise
move on his part, taking into consideration the
"realities of the situation". It will be recalled
that in December, 1937 the offices of the "Novosti
Dnia" were subjected to a bomb attack, presumably,
by a pro-Japanese group of local Russians. In
April 1940, alarmed by a series of anonymous
telephone calls generally abusing him and
threatening to send him an "Easter present" for
his anti-Japanese campaign in connection with
the recent municipal elections, he applied for
Police protection.
page_data.zh:
- 11 -

随着欧洲当前战争的爆发，《今日新闻》 sharply 改变了对德国的态度，并且是上海唯一突出报道跨洋通讯社（Transocean Agency）新闻的俄文报纸。然而，最近明显出现了倾向于法国和英国的变化。

可以肯定的是，除其他外，奇利金是日本人不受欢迎的人（persona non grata），而且他完全清楚这一点。因此，在过去几个月里，《今日新闻》的反日态度逐渐淡化。考虑到“局势的现实”，这似乎是他非常明智的举动。回想起来，1937年12月，《今日新闻》的办公室遭到炸弹袭击，推测是由当地亲日的俄国人群体所为。1940年4月，由于接到一系列匿名电话，一般性地辱骂他并威胁要因其最近在市政选举相关的反日运动而送他一份“复活节礼物”，他感到恐慌，遂申请警方保护。

page_data.en:
- 12 -

Rumours have been circulating for the
past few months that Chilikin intends to sell his
paper and to depart from Shanghai. Latest
information indicates that some time towards the
end of June last he sold the "Novosti Dnia" to
the "Moscow Narodny Bank" and it is reported that,
beginning from 28-7-40, it will be conducted
as a purely Soviet newspaper.

----------
page_data.zh:
- 12 -

过去几个月流传着谣言，称奇利金打算出售他的报纸并离开上海。最新信息显示，去年6月底左右，他将《今日新闻》出售给了“莫斯科国民银行”（Moscow Narodny Bank），据报道，从1940年7月28日开始，该报将作为纯粹的苏联报纸运营。

----------

page_data.en:
August 21, 1937.

Kong Chan (抗戰), a three-day periodical, published
the following article on August 19 :-

LETTER FROM RUSSIAN DAILY NEWS TO MADAME SUN YAT-SEN

(Editor's note: The following is a letter sent
by the Russian Daily News (俄文每日新聞), a local
newspaper established by White Russians, to Madame
Sun Yat-sen expressing their sympathy with China's
resistance. It will be seen that the Japanese
Imperialists are common enemies of the world.)

"Madame Sun Yat-sen,

"Please allow us to use the name of the
Russian Daily News to express our greatest sympathy
at this time of China's crisis.

"We must now explain the rumour current in
various circles of China to the effect that White
Russians living in China are joining hands with the
Japanese. This is completely erroneous because the
majority of White Russians living in China, especially
those residing in Shanghai, would never do anything
to harm China. We are preparing to join hands with
China and fight against the enemy of China and Russia.

"For a long time the greatest enemy of Russia
has been Japan. Japan has sent spies to Russian and
has continued to cause trouble on the boundary of
Russia She oppresses Russians and Chinese in
'Manchukuo'.

"Although our paper has been in circulation
for many years, yet this is the first time that we
have given a sincere explanation to the Chinese people.
We will not change our attitude towards China and
will continue to resist the enemies of China and
Russia.

"Russian residents in Shanghai all sympathize
with China. Only a small number of shameless elements
and newspapers connected with 'Manchukuo' impair
the friendly relations between China and Russia.

"Russia and China are both at present facing
the terror of fighting and foreign interference. This
will only strengthen the consolidation of the Russian
people. We believe that in the present critical
situation, China will become still more united.

"Our unchangeable slogan is: 'China and
Russia are friendly to each other and will join and
assist mutually in the struggle against the Japanese
Imperialists!'

"The Russian Daily News,
"No. 480 Prince Edward
"August 19."
page_data.zh:
1937年8月21日。

《抗战》（Kong Chan），一份三日刊，于8月19日刊登了以下文章：

《俄文每日新闻》致孙夫人函

（编者按：下文系由白俄在当地创办的报纸《俄文每日新闻》（Russian Daily News）致孙夫人的一封信，表达其对中国抗战的同情。由此可见，日本帝国主义者是世界共同的敌人。）

“孙夫人：

“请允许我们以《俄文每日新闻》的名义，在中国处于危机之际，表达我们最深切的同情。

“我们必须现在就中国各界流传的一种谣言作出解释，该谣言称在华白俄正与日本人勾结。这完全是错误的，因为在华白俄，尤其是居住在上海的白俄，绝不会做任何损害中国的事情。我们正准备与中国携手，共同对抗中国和俄罗斯的敌人。

“长期以来，俄罗斯最大的敌人一直是日本。日本向俄罗斯派遣间谍，并继续在俄罗斯边境制造麻烦。他们在‘满洲国’压迫俄罗斯人和中国人。

“虽然本报已发行多年，但这是我们第一次向中国人民作出真诚的说明。我们对中国的态度不会改变，并将继续抵抗中国和俄罗斯的敌人。

“在上海的俄罗斯居民都同情中国。只有少数无耻之徒以及与‘满洲国’有关的报纸破坏了中俄之间的友好关系。

“俄罗斯和中国目前都面临着战争的恐怖和外国的干涉。这只会加强俄罗斯人民的团结。我们相信，在目前的危急局势下，中国将更加团结。

“我们不变的口号是：‘中俄友好，携手互助，共同抗击日本帝国主义者！’

“《俄文每日新闻》
“爱德华王子路480号
“8月19日”

The Russian Daily News, formerly owned by Mr. V.A.
Chilikin, which recently changed hands and became the
property of the Moscow Narodny Bank and the local
official organ of the Soviet Government will, for the first
time, appear on the streets on July 24th. 1940 printed in
the new Russian orthography as a Special Anniversary
Edition devoted to the Soviet Navy.
The services of Mr. Chilikin as editor of the
newspaper are still retained by the new management so as
to keep secret for the time being the fact that the
newspaper has changed hands.
No confirmation is as yet available of the report
that Mr. Chilikin is leaving Shanghai for Honolulu,
Hawaii where it was stated he would spend a vacation in
the company of Mme Greenhouse, an intimate friend of his.
Mr. Chilikin has not yet applied to the local U.S.
Consulate-General for a visa to visit Hawaii.
The report also stated that he would travel to
Chungking either before or after his visit to Hawaii in
order to see Mr. Panoushkin, Soviet Ambassador to China.
However no indication of what route he will take to the
War Capital is available.

Made by D.S.I. Maklaevsky Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

（批：D.C. (Sp. Br.)）
（批：Copies to E(2) Z. R.J. 30/6 Sent PM 27/6）
（印：H sent 27/6）
（印：27 JUNE 1940 COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）
（印：FILE）

Information has been received from a very reliable source to the effect that a pro-Soviet Newspaper " The Russian Daily News " owned and edited by Mr. V.A.Chilikin was, on Saturday June the 22nd. 1940, sold to the Moscow Narodny Bank. The price is believed to be around U.S.$ 10.000.00.

During negotiations the Soviet side was represented by Mr. Zephiroff, Senior Book - keeper of the Moscow Narodny Bank and by Mr. M.A. Brunner, unofficial representative of the Soviet Trade Mission in Chungking ( Torgpredstvo ) while the newspaper was represented by Mr. Chilikin and Mr. Veiss, Editor.

The paper will retain its present name but will become an Official organ of the Soviet Government. It will be controlled by Messrs Bernoff and Vyhriaeff of the local TASS Agency and its business side will be in the hands of the Moscow Narodny Bank.

The policy of the new paper will reflect that of the Soviet Government and it is believed that it will be definitely anti-British.

It will support the policy of the German Government and will work in a close cooperation with the local branch of the Transocean News Agency and the German

新报纸的政策将反映苏联政府的立场，据信其将明确持反英态度。

Subject "Novosti Dnia" ( Russian Daily News ).

Made by D.S.L. Prokofiev.    Forwarded by [Signature]

The daily newspaper in the Russian language entitled
"NOVOSTI DNIA" ( Russian Daily News ) was established in the
French Concession in March, 1933 and from August, 1935 its edi-
torial and printing offices have been located at 620 Avenue Foch
in the Settlement. It is edited and published by V.A. Chilikin
who is reported to have started his journalistic career in Mos-
cow about twenty years ago.

Originally intended to be a "non-political, non-party
and absolutely independent newspaper of Russian emigrants" the
"Novosti Dnia" in 1936 gradually adopted a pro-Soviet attitude.
During the course of 1937 this attitude has become so pronounced
that this newspaper may now be regarded as a successor to the lo-
cal Soviet newspaper "China Daily Herald" which ceased publica-
tion on October 1st, 1937. Together with this political evolution
developed the anti-Japanese tendencies of this newspaper which
reached their culminating point during the present Sino-Japanese
hostilities.

The editor of the "Novosti Dnia" came to the notice
of the French police in 1935 in connection with his blackmailing
activities and was warned to discontinue them. The "Novosti Dnia"
also became notorious on account of its vicious attacks on various
organizations and individual members of the local Russian commu-
nity. The scandalous campaigns conducted from time to time by
V.A. Chilikin in connection with various matters relating to the
inner life of that community invariably created an atmosphere of
ill-feeling and animosity on account of the reckless and vulgar
manner they were carried out and very often went beyond the li-
mits of common decency.

In September, 1935 the "Novosti Dnia" was banned in

这份名为“NOVOSTI DNIA”（《俄文每日新闻》）的俄文日报于1933年3月在法租界创办，自1935年8月起，其编辑部和印刷所位于租界内的福煦路620号。该报由 V.A. Chilikin 编辑和出版，据报道，他约二十年前在莫斯科开始了其新闻职业生涯。

《Novosti Dnia》最初旨在成为一份“非政治、非党派且绝对独立的俄罗斯移民报纸”，但在1936年逐渐采取了亲苏态度。在1937年期间，这种态度变得如此明显，以至于该报现在可被视为当地已于1937年10月1日停刊的苏联报纸《China Daily Herald》的继任者。随着这一政治演变，该报的反日倾向也得以发展，并在当前的中日敌对行动中达到了顶峰。

《Novosti Dnia》的编辑在1935年因其勒索活动引起法国警方的注意，并被警告停止此类活动。《Novosti Dnia》还因对当地俄罗斯社区的各种组织和个人成员进行恶毒攻击而声名狼藉。V.A. Chilikin 不时就该社区内部生活的各种事项发起的丑闻运动，由于其鲁莽和 vulgar（粗俗）的方式进行， invariably（总是）制造了不和与敌意的氛围，并且经常超出一般体面的界限。

1935年9月，《Novosti Dnia》在

the French Concession for publishing articles containing sarcas-

ban was lifted only after the newspaper published a full apology
for the article in question.
        From December, 1936 to September, 1937 the "Novosti
Dnia" came officially to the notice of the Municipal Police on no
less than ten different occasions in connection with either com-
plaints lodged against the editor or against objectionable and
untruthful articles published in this newspaper. Warnings by the
Police to refrain from continuing with articles of this nature re-
mained unheeded and consequently, the "Novosti Dnia" was closed
by the Police on September 8, 1937, under the Emergency Orders. The
ban was removed on 28-9-37 after Mr. Chilikin had given an un-
dertaking " in good faith to refrain from publishing objectionable
or abusive matter of any kind". So far this undertaking has been
carried out.
        Information from reliable sources indicates that both
the capital and the circulation of the "Novosti Dnia" are greatly
overstated in the attached registration form. The capital of the
newspaper is estimated at about $10,000 and its circulation is re-
ported not to exceed 1,000 copies at present. It is generally
believed that the "Novosti Dnia" is subsidized by the local Soviet
authorities and that the formation in January, 1937 of the "Russian
Publishing Company" of which Mr. Chilikin is Managing Director,
is merely a bluff and possibly a screen for covering the subsi-
dy.

                                A. Prokofiev

法租界因其刊登包含讽刺批评法公董局政策的文章而对其实施禁令。该报就有关文章刊登完整道歉声明后，禁令方予解除。
        从1936年12月至1937年9月，《Novosti Dnia》（音译）因针对其编辑的投诉或该报刊登的令人反感及不实文章，至少十次正式引起工部局警务处的注意。警方警告其停止刊登此类文章，但未获理会，因此，警务处于1937年9月8日根据《紧急命令》关闭了《Novosti Dnia》（音译）。在Chilikin先生（音译）作出“诚意保证不再刊登任何令人反感或辱骂性内容”后，禁令于1937年9月28日解除。迄今为止，该保证已得到履行。
        来自可靠渠道的消息表明，所附登记表中所列《Novosti Dnia》（音译）的资本和发行量均被大大夸大。估计该报资本约为10,000美元，目前发行量据报道不超过1,000份。人们普遍认为，《Novosti Dnia》（音译）由当地苏维埃当局资助，而Chilikin先生（音译）任总经理的“俄罗斯出版公司”于1937年1月成立，仅仅是一种虚张声势，可能是掩盖资助的幌子。

Subject (in full) Sunday Mercury - Application for re-registration

Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Forwarded herewith is an application for
re-registration of the Sunday Mercury, a weekly
supplement of the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury,
with Mr. A.L. Meyer as Editor. Mr. Meyer, who is also
a U.S. citizen and resides at 640 Avenue Foch, succeeds
Mr. Randall Gould who has left for U.S.A.

The policy of the publication will remain as
heretofore and the change will not affect the conduct
of the paper in any way and Mr. Randall Gould will still
maintain a connection with the publication.

Certificate No.F.59 issued in the name of
Mr. Randall Gould is forwarded for classification.

（签名）
A. C. (Special Branch).

（签名：D. S. I. Young）
D. S. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
S.5, Special Branch Added,
REPORT    Date July 13, 1939.
Subject Publications of Post Mercury Company - Application for renewal.

Made by    and    Forwarded by D.S. Pharazyn

x Renewed 7/7

With reference to the attached letter dated July 12,
1939, from the Post Mercury Company, the Registration
Certificates Nos. F.21 and F.59 in respect of the
"Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury" and the "Sunday
Mercury" are duly renewed.

Duplicates for Registration Certificates Nos. C.44
and F.45 for the "Ta Mei Wan Pao" (大美晚報) and the "Ta
Mei Pictorial" have been prepared and are attached
herewith for favour of signature of D.C. (Special Branch),
the original ones being claimed to have been mislaid or
lost.

Instructions of D.C. (Special Branch) are solicited
as how to deal with the Registration Certificates Nos.
C.166 and F.38 in respect of the "Ta Mei Pao" (大美報)
and the "China in Pictures," as the former, which is a
Chinese language daily, has suspended publication since
May 19, 1939, while the latter has been amalgamated
with the "Ta Mei Pictorial" (Certificate F.45).

It is also respectfully suggested that an application
form for the "Ta Mei Chou Pao," a weekly paper in Chinese
appearing every Sunday, be forwarded to the Post Mercury
Company to be filled in, as this paper is not registered
with the S.M.C.

（左侧手写批注：）
9/5
See Post in re
& stand C.166 & F.38 as
now unnecessary. Arrange for
ticket for ta mei pao
after known from D.
When taken over
HP?

D. S. Pharazyn
D. S.

D. C. (Special Branch)

Subject. Shanghai Municipality Private Broadcasting Stations' Guild -
Application for registration
Made by. D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by. C. Gauson
* See also D 6813/14/II
With reference to the attached application
dated August 16 from the Shanghai Municipality
Private Broadcasting Stations' Guild, Room 6A,
119 Nanking Road, for registration, enquiries show
that the formation of this guild was promoted and
sponsored by the Radio Broadcasting Control Office
(Japanese) with a view to facilitating control of
those broadcasting stations which had registered
with this organ. Out of a total of 39 broad-
casting stations in Shanghai, twenty-eight have
joined this guild, the remaining eleven being
purely Japanese or with foreign interests.
According to Soong Chih ( 宋杰 ), the
nominal Chairman of the guild, Major K. Asano, Chief
of the Radio Broadcasting Control Office, will
direct all the activities of the Guild and he will
only be responsible for passing on Major Asano's
instructions to the members. Soong Chih is
otherwise known as Soong Dz-siang ( 宋士驤 ), a
lawyer by profession, living at 4 Van Ziang Li
( 萬祥里 ), Elgin Road, (Tel. 41925). He is
a leading member in the Special District Office of
the Shanghai Municipality Ricsha Owners' Association,
81 Lloyd Road and also a committee member of the
1st Special District Citizens' Federation, 406
Kiangse Road. He is concurrently Manager of the
Dah Yah Broadcasting Station, 545 Kiukiang Road,
which is supported financially by a number of the

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. REGISTRY
No. S948t Date 19/9/40
51512
Shanghai Jewish Chronicle - Gelbe Post - Deported emigrants

On 20.9.40 a letter was received from Mr. Paul
Komor, Hon. Sec. of the International Committee for the
Organization of European Immigrants in China to the
effect that the Gelbe Post had been acquired by the
Shanghai Jewish Chronicle. The writer goes on to
say that there is no room for more than one local
immigrant morning paper and adds that he has now heard
that an application has been made to this office by
Mr. Horst Lewin, Mr. Wolff and the English wife of
a German Immigrant for re-registration of the Gelbe
Post.

So far as this office is aware the present
position and history of the two papers is as follows:-
Shanghai Jewish Chronicle was first registered
with S.M. Police in the name of Mr. Osias Lewin as
Editor, Publisher and Proprietor and Registration
Certificate issued on 26.4.39.

Gelbe Post was first registered in the name of
Adolf Josef Storfer, Editor, Publisher and Proprietor
on 17.8.39 as a semi-monthly, was changed to a bi-
weekly in January 1940 and to a daily in February 1940.

On 26.8.40 a letter was received from
Mr. Storfer to the effect that he had sold all his
rights in the publication to Osias Lewin and a similar
letter from Mr. Lewin stating he had purchased the
paper.

On September 3, 1940, Mr. O. Lewin called at
this office and made application for re-registration

also See

51512
《上海犹太纪事报》- 《黄报》- 被驱逐的移民

1940年9月20日，收到在华欧洲移民组织国际委员会荣誉秘书保罗·科莫尔（Paul Komor）先生来信，称《黄报》（Gelbe Post）已被《上海犹太纪事报》收购。写信人接着说，当地容不下一份以上的移民晨报，并补充说他现在听说，霍斯特·莱温（Horst Lewin）先生、沃尔夫（Wolff）先生以及一位德国移民的英国妻子已向本处申请重新注册《黄报》。

据本处所知，这两家报纸目前的状况和历史如下：-
《上海犹太纪事报》最初以奥西亚斯·莱温（Osias Lewin）先生为编辑、出版商和业主的名义在上海公共租界警务处注册，注册证书于1939年4月26日签发。

《黄报》最初于1939年8月17日以阿道夫·约瑟夫·斯托弗（Adolf Josef Storfer）为编辑、出版商和业主的名义注册为半月刊，1940年1月改为双周刊，1940年2月改为日报。

1940年8月26日，收到斯托弗先生来信，称他已将其在该出版物中的所有权利出售给奥西亚斯·莱温，并收到莱温先生类似的来信，声明他已购买该报。

1940年9月3日，O. 莱温先生来到本处，申请重新注册

17 CANTON ROAD
SHANGHAI, CHINA
April 9th, 1940.

Commissioner of the Police
Shanghai Municipal Council
185, Foochow Road
SHANGHAI

Sir,

As publisher and editor of the daily newspaper "Gelbe Post" (17, Canton Rd.), duly registered with the S.M.P. under the number F-62, and as a ratepayer of the International Settlement, I beg to draw your attention to the following:

Today, on Monday, April 6, in the forenoon, there appeared in the part of Shanghai lying north of Soochow Creek several persons dressed in black, apparently of the Japanese nationality, and visited a number of shops in which copies of "Gelbe Post" were displayed for sale. They energetically demanded that the shop owners should hand over to them all the issues of the above named paper, such demand being granted in all instances.

The shop owners tried to question these persons as to
1) their identity,
2) on whose behalf they were acting and
3) the reason for their doings,
but not a single of the above questions was answered and also
4) no receipts were issued against the delivery of the paper.

Furthermore, I was informed by several street sellers that they were held up by persons in Japanese uniforms and that all issues of the "Gelbe Post" which they had on hand were taken away without stating any reasons and without any receipts.

I have been waiting that in the course of the day some information would be forthcoming to me, or to the office of the "Gelbe Post", 17, Canton Road, which would help me to clarify this entirely mysterious and unreasonable seizure of my newspaper, but up to this moment, viz., 5 p.m. no such information is to hand, and I am not sure that tomorrow's issues will not suffer the same fate.

I feel compelled to bring the above occurrences to the knowledge of the S.M.P. and reserve my rights to claim damages suffered on account of the above.

I remain, Sir,

Your obedient servant
A.J. Storfer
Publisher and Editor
of the
"GELBE POST"

作为日报《黄报》（广东路17号）的出版商和编辑，该报已在上海公共租界警务处正式注册，编号为 F-62，且本人系国际公共租界纳税人，我谨提请阁下注意以下事项：

今天，即4月6日星期一上午，在苏州河以北的上海地区，出现了几名身穿黑衣、看似日本国籍的人，他们走访了多家展示出售《黄报》的商店。他们强力要求店主交出上述报纸的所有期数，所有店主均照办。

店主们试图询问这些人：
1) 他们的身份，
2) 他们代表谁行事，以及
3) 他们这样做的原因，
但上述问题均未得到回答，而且
4) 在交付报纸时未开具任何收据。

此外，几名街头报贩告诉我，他们被身穿日本制服的人拦下，手中所有的《黄报》都被拿走，未说明任何理由，也未开具任何收据。

我一直在等待当天能收到一些信息，或发给位于广东路17号的《黄报》办公室的信息，以帮助我澄清这次对我报纸完全神秘且不合理的查扣，但截至此刻，即下午5点，尚未收到此类信息，我也不确定明天的期数是否会遭受同样的命运。

我觉得有必要将上述事件告知上海公共租界警务处，并保留就上述原因遭受损失提出索赔的权利。

此致

您的顺从仆人

CHINA PRESS.
APR 9 1940

Japanese Seize Emigre
Papers

Refugees' Stand In
Election Believed
Cause Of Seizure

Squads of Japanese in plainclothes "invaded" Hongkew newsstands yesterday and seized all the copies of the German refugee paper, the Gelbe Post (Yellow Post).

The order for confiscation was apparently issued after the refugee daily had intimated in its recent editions that the emigres in Shanghai should help other Occidentals in preserving the status quo on the Shanghai Municipal Council during the forthcoming elections.

Immediately following the seizure of the paper, Mr. A. J. Storfer, editor and publisher of the refugee daily, lodged a written protest with the Commissioner of Police.

It was asserted that at about 8 a.m. yesterday, Japanese squads cruised through Hongkew's streets in cars and stopped at every store or newsstand selling the paper. Shopkeepers declared that no reason was given by the men for the confiscation. Newsboys hawking the papers on the streets were also relieved of their issues, it was declared. No attempt was made by S.M.P. officers to halt the confiscation, it was said.

No payment for the confiscated papers, totalling about 1,000 copies selling at 10 cents each, was made. However, newsboys south of the creek sold their papers with the slogan: "Extra—Extra—Confiscated in Hongkew!"

A few hours later Major K. M. Bourne, S.M.P. Commissioner met with high Japanese officials and discussed the "Hitler return" incident north of the creek to S.M.P. control. No announcement was forthcoming yesterday as to the progress or results of the discussion. Among the points which were to be considered are included the number of Police officers to be stationed in the areas, the posts they will assume, and the composition of the newly-created "E" division.

Democracies Lauded

In several issues in the past week, the paper has printed articles on the coming elections in which the Governments of America, Britain, and France were lauded. Although no direct appeal was made for the emigres to vote for the seven "authorized" British and American candidates as opposed to the Japanese candidates, Japanese authorities allegedly were angered at "between-the-lines" inferences.

One article warned readers that those emigres who abstain from voting would be helping the Japanese cause. Another article declared that refugees must not only be thankful for having escaped the Third Reich, but also that they are allowed in Shanghai to uphold their own opinions of Nazism. "Our hopes are connected with the three great Democracies," it was stated, "and we are lucky to be able to live here where representatives of those Powers have such a large part in the administration of the city."

日本人查抄流亡者报刊

据信难民在选举中的立场是查抄原因

昨日，便衣日本小队“闯入”虹口报摊，查抄了德国难民报纸《黄色邮报》（Gelbe Post，即 Yellow Post）的所有副本。

没收令显然是在该难民日报最近几期刊文暗示上海的流亡者应在即将到来的选举中帮助其他西方人维持上海公共租界工部局的现状之后发布的。

报纸被查抄后，《黄色邮报》主编兼出版人 A. J. Storfer 先生立即向警务处处长提交了书面抗议。

据称，昨日上午8时左右，日本小队乘车在虹口街道巡逻，并在每一家出售该报的商店或报摊前停下。店主声称，这些人未给出任何查抄理由。据称，在街上叫卖报纸的报童也被收缴了所售报纸。据说，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）警官未试图阻止查抄行动。

对于被没收的约1,000份报纸（每份售价10分），未支付任何款项。然而，苏州河以南的报童在售卖报纸时高呼：“号外——号外——虹口遭查抄！”

数小时后，上海公共租界工部局警务处处长 K. M. Bourne 少校与日本高级官员会面，讨论了苏州河以北地区发生的“希特勒归来”事件移交警务处管辖一事。昨日并未发布关于讨论进展或结果的公告。待议事项包括将在该地区部署的警员人数、他们将担任的岗位，以及新成立的“E”区的组成人员。

赞扬民主国家

在过去一周的几期报纸中，该报刊登了关于即将举行的选举的文章，赞扬了美国、英国和法国政府。虽然并未直接呼吁流亡者投票支持七位“获授权”的英美候选人以反对日本候选人，但据称日本当局对文章中的“弦外之音”感到愤怒。

一篇文章警告读者，那些 abstain from voting（放弃投票）的流亡者将有助于日本的事业。另一篇文章宣称，难民不仅应感激自己逃脱了第三帝国，还应感激他们被允许在上海坚持自己对纳粹主义的看法。文中 stated（陈述）：“我们的希望与三大民主国家紧密相连，我们很幸运能生活在这里，这些大国的代表在城市管理中发挥着如此重要的作用。”

Storfer 先生在致警务处处长的信中写道：

“作为日报《黄色邮报》（广东路17号）的出版人和编辑，该报已按编号 F-62 在上海公共租界工部局正式注册，且本人系国际公共租界的纳税人，谨提请阁下注意以下事项：

“今日，即4月8日星期一上午，在苏州河以北的上海地区，出现了几名身穿黑衣、看似日本国籍的人，他们走访了多家展示出售《黄色邮报》的商店。他们强力要求店主交出上述报纸的所有期号，这一要求在所有情况下均得到满足。

“店主曾试图询问这些人：
1) 他们的身份，
2) 他们代表谁行事，以及
3) 他们这样做的原因；
但上述问题均未得到回答，并且
4) 在交付报纸时未开具任何收据。

“此外，我获悉几名街头小贩被身穿日本制服的人拦截，他们随身携带的所有《黄色邮报》均被无理由拿走……”

Thanks Said Due
The Gelbe Fest, however, also
printed an article which said that
many thanks were due the Japanese
"who have put no obstacles in our
path."
A Jewish committee appeal to
emigres to remain neutral in the
election controversy, and not to vote
at all because of the risk of making
enemies, was reprinted in the daily.
This effort to placate the Japanese
was unsuccessful, it was asserted,
and the request not to cast any bal-
lot at all was apparently taken as
a hostile act, it was said.
America in particular was praised
by the emigre journal, which point-
ed out that money from the Boxer
Indemnity fund had been turned
back to build schools and hospitals
in China, and that it had fostered
an era of peaceful and prosperous
relations between the Orient and
Occident.

Other Methods
Other methods by Japanese autho-
rities to grasp control of the emigre
vote were also charged, with the
allegation that already, many refu-
gees in Hongkew who had promised
to vote for the Japanese candidates
had received passes which would al-
low relatives, family or friends still
in Europe to come to Shanghai.
Some persons, it was alleged, who
had no need of the passes, were raf-
fling them off, and in some cases
received as much as $1,000 for the
sale of a single pass.
A Japanese election office has also
been set up in Hongkew, where
several Japanese speaking fluent
German are stumping for the five
candidates Retaliation was threaten-
ed, it was alleged, if the refugees
did not vote for the Japanese in
the forthcoming elections.
However, many observers wonder-
ed yesterday how effective this
threat of retaliation would be, since
the ballot is supposed to be a secret
one, and unless underhanded me-
thods were used, it would be dif-
ficult to discover how an individual
voted in the elections.

Anti-British Pamphlets
Another means by which the
election campaign for support of
the minorities is being carried on
was reported yesterday in the shape
of pamphlets, printed in Russian.
Purpose of these was to sway the
Russian vote from the "Anglo-
Saxon" candidates and to the
Japanese candidates, it was said.
Blatantly anti-British, the pam-
phlets, distributed on Avenue Joffre
Saturday night by unemployed
Russians, told the Russian com-
munity not to be "a small puppy
dog kissing the hand of those who
beat you."
Calling the "present" designated
"first gentlemen" and the previous
"second settlement," the pamphlet
urges the community not to be led
by the S.M.O. which demands
of its money and fails to give
assistance when the Crisis was
at hand.
The pamphlet was signed by the
Russian Group of Shanghai, which
is believed to be a Japanese-sponsored
organization.

致谢之辞
然而，《黄色邮报》也刊登了一篇文章，称应当
向日本人致以许多谢意，因为他们“没有在我们的道路上设置障碍”。
该日报还转载了一个犹太委员会呼吁流亡者在选举争议中保持中立、因担心树敌而完全不要投票的请求。据称，这种安抚日本人的努力并未成功，据说完全不投票的请求反而被视为一种敌对行为。
该流亡者刊物特别赞扬了美国，指出庚子赔款基金的资金已被退还用于在中国建设学校和医院，并且它促进了一个东方与西方和平繁荣关系的时代。

其他手段
还有人指控日本当局采取了其他手段来控制流亡者的选票，据称虹口许多已承诺投票给日本候选人的难民已经获得了通行证，这些通行证将允许仍留在欧洲的亲属、家人或朋友前来上海。据称，一些并不需要这些通行证的人正在抽奖分发它们，在某些情况下，单张通行证的售价高达1,000美元。
虹口还设立了一个日本选举办公室，几名讲流利德语的日本人在那里为五位候选人进行拉票活动。据称，如果难民不在即将到来的选举中投票给日本人，就会受到报复威胁。
然而，许多观察家昨日怀疑这种报复威胁的有效性，因为投票本应是秘密的，除非使用不正当手段，否则很难发现个人在选举中是如何投票的。

反英宣传册
昨日有报道指出，争取少数族裔支持的竞选活动的另一种手段是以俄语印刷的宣传册形式进行的。据说，这些宣传册的目的是将俄罗斯人的选票从“盎格鲁-撒克逊”候选人转向日本候选人。
这些宣传册公然反英，周六晚由失业的俄罗斯人在霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）分发，告诫俄罗斯社区不要做“亲吻打你之手的小哈巴狗”。
该宣传册将现任指定人员称为“第一绅士”，将前任称为“第二租界”，敦促社区不要被上海公共租界工部局（S.M.O.，原文如此，应为 S.M.C. 或指代市政机构）所引导，该机构索要钱财却在危机迫在眉睫时未能提供援助。
该宣传册由“上海俄罗斯团体”署名，该团体被认为是一个由日本赞助的组织。

CHINA DAILY NEWS
APR 9 1940

Japanese Seize
Jewish Paper

Readers Urged To
Remain Aloof of
Local Politics

All copies of the "Gelbe Post,"
newest addition to the German-
language Jewish refugee press in
Shanghai, were confiscated by the
Japanese yesterday morning when
employees of the newspaper were
about to commence distribution to
subscribers living north of Soochow
Creek.

In the leading article appearing in
Sunday's issue of the paper, the
progress of Shanghai ever since the
first Britons set foot here is borne
out and particular emphasis is laid
on the wonderful work put in by
British, French and American
initiative during the past many
years in making Shanghai the
important centre it is today.

With reference to the Japanese,
the writer of the article states that
the refugees must be thankful to
them not only for permitting them
to live in areas in which the Japanese
have exercised certain executive
control since it became necessary
for them to land troops here as a
result of the hostilities near Shanghai,
but also, that they have in many
instances been most helpful to the
refugees who are participating in
the reconstruction of those areas.

Letter to Police Commissioner

In a written communication to the
Commissioner of Police the publishers
of the "Gelbe Post" yesterday point-
ed out that a number of persons dres-
sed in black, apparently of Japanese
nationality, had demanded the handing
over of all copies of the newspaper
on sale in a number of shops. In
each instance the demands had been
complied with.

The communication added that shop
owners had attempted to ques-
tion these persons as to their iden-
tity, on whose behalf they were
acting and the reason for their
action. It further pointed out that
no receipts were issued for the
delivery of the papers. Further-
more several street vendors were
held up by persons in Japanese
uniform and all issues of the "Gelbe
Post" were taken away from them,
the missive stated.

In alluding to local politics no
word is said about the forthcoming
elections—the writer urges readers
not to side with any faction or party
and to remain outside the political
arena which, he contends, concerns
only those who have lived in
Shanghai here and who have been
identified for many years with
the city's municipal life.

《大美晚报》
1940年4月9日

日本人查抄犹太报纸

呼吁读者远离本地政治

昨日早晨，当《黄色邮报》的员工正准备开始向居住在苏州河以北的订阅者分发报纸时，该报所有副本均被日本人查抄。《黄色邮报》是上海德语犹太难民报刊中最新的成员。

在该报周日刊发的社论中，证实了自第一批英国人踏足此地以来上海的进步，并特别强调了过去多年来英国、法国和美国的努力在使上海成为今天这样的重要中心方面所做出的卓越工作。

关于日本人，该文作者指出，难民必须感谢他们，不仅是因为允许他们生活在日本人自因上海附近战事必要而派兵登陆以来行使了一定行政控制的区域，而且在许多情况下，日本人对参与这些地区重建的难民提供了极大帮助。

致警务处处长的信

《黄色邮报》出版人昨日在致警务处处长的书面函件中指出，数名身穿黑衣、看似日本国籍的人要求交出在多家商店出售的所有报纸副本。在每种情况下，这一要求都得到了遵从。

该函件补充说，店主曾试图询问这些人的身份、他们代表谁行事以及他们采取行动的原因。函件进一步指出，交付报纸时未开具任何收据。此外，该信函称，几名街头小贩被身穿日本制服的人拦截，他们所有的《黄色邮报》期号均被拿走。

在提及本地政治时，只字未提即将到来的选举——作者敦促读者不要站队任何派系或政党，并远离政治舞台，他认为政治舞台只关乎那些长期居住在上海并与城市市政生活息息相关多年的人。

Gelbe Post - Seizure by Japanese

Forwarded herewith are newspaper cuttings from
the North-China Daily News and China Press of April
9, 1940, dealing with the seizure in areas North
of the Soochow Creek, by Japanese, of copies of the
April 8th issue of the Gelbe Post, Jewish emigre

In addition attached are 5 copies of a translation
from the German of an article appearing in the April 8th
issue of the Gelbe Post and to which certain objection
was raised.

Certified true copy

JBS.

SHANGHAI AND THREE GREAT DEMOCRACIES
GREAT BRITAIN, FRANCE AND U.S.A.
...........
A FEW WORDS TO NEW ARRIVALS

This week about 100 new central Europeans
arrived in Shanghai. They come from the original Germany
and its newly added "territories" and "protectorates".
Many of us who for many months already
have been away from the swastika-hell, are maybe inclined
somewhat to forget, what we went through in the past.
Whoever has left Germany or Austria since 1938, and
Czechoslovakia and Poland since 1939, already had nothing
more to lose and even the fact that he could flee the
power-sphere of Adolf Hitler was a gain for him.
It would be thanklessness without precedent
to ever forget what fortune it was to be rescued from the
claws of the brown dictatorship, and if we think of those who
have not had this fortune, or not as yet, we must admit that
all our personal miseries which still exist must stand far
behind in importance those facing people who are still in the
Third Reich.
Emigrants from Central Europe are to be found
in many countries and several continents. Shanghai is by no
means the most important emigrant centre, nevertheless it is
one of the bigger ones. In one respect, however, Shanghai is
unique as an emigrant centre. It belongs neither to those
territories where immigration leads to naturalization (as for
instance in the United States and the Argentine), nor to the
transit territories where refugees have not the right of making
a living but where they mark time prior to emigrating
page_data.zh:
上海与三大民主国家
大不列颠、法兰西和美利坚合众国
...........
致新来者的几句话

本周约有100名中欧新人抵达上海。他们来自原德国及其新增的“领土”和“保护国”。我们中许多人已经离开卐字地狱数月之久，或许倾向于 somewhat（稍微）忘记我们过去的经历。自1938年以来离开德国或奥地利，以及自1939年以来离开捷克斯洛伐克和波兰的人，已经没有什么可失去的了，甚至能够逃离阿道夫·希特勒的势力范围对他们来说也是一种收获。
如果永远忘记从棕色独裁统治的魔爪中被解救出来是何等幸运，那将是前所未有的忘恩负义；如果我们想到那些没有这种运气、或者尚未拥有这种运气的人，我们必须承认，我们个人目前仍存在的苦难，与那些仍在第三帝国的人们所面临的苦难相比，其重要性相去甚远。
中欧移民分布在许多国家和几个大陆。上海绝非最重要的移民中心，尽管如此，它仍是较大的移民中心之一。然而，在一个方面，上海作为移民中心是独特的。它既不属于那些移民导致归化的领土（例如在美国和阿根廷），也不属于那些难民无权谋生、只能在移民前消磨时间的过境领土

page_data.en:

elsewhere (as for example Switzerland), nor does it belong
to the type of emigrant territory such as France, where
emigrants have the choice of being considered enemy aliens
watched and perhaps interned, or to profess themselves as
political refugees, and to side with the immigration-country
and possibly do military service.
To none of these types of emigrant territories
does Shanghai belong. In this city of China, the right of
earning and of settling is given to all foreigners by virtue of
old treaties. As a result of tens of years, present conditions
have come to prevail, i.e. that France has jurisdiction over
her own Concession while for all other foreigners the International
Settlement has been created.
The originators of the Foreign Settlement were
the Englishmen, who 98 years ago created the basis for the
commercial and industrial centre which Shanghai is to-day.
Shanghai owes its present condition mainly to
British perseverance and British diligence, British
circumspection and the British gift for organization.
Britons like all other foreigners, are not
"masters" here in the true sense, and what they have constructed
in visible and invisible accomplishments they did not do as
empire-builders, and the Foreign Settlements, which is
erroneously referred-to as "British" is in no way part of the
Empire. Britons too, like everyone else here except the
Chinese, are only guests, although they are guests enjoying a
hospitality having a certain contractorial basis. Nevertheless,
even as guests they have accomplished a tremendous amount,
practically wonders, for their hosts, the Chinese.
France has a large Far Eastern possession in
Indo-China. Apart from this, however, her interests are very

其他地方（例如瑞士）也不属于那种移民领土类型，如法国，在那里的移民可以选择被视为受监视并可能被拘禁的敌国侨民，或者宣称自己是政治难民，站在移居国一边并可能服兵役。
上海不属于上述任何一种类型的移民领土。在这座中国城市里，凭借旧条约，所有外国人都享有谋生和定居的权利。经过数十年的演变，形成了目前的局面，即法国对其自身的租界拥有管辖权，而为所有其他外国人则设立了公共租界。
外人租界的创始者是英国人，他们在98年前为上海今日成为工商业中心奠定了基础。
上海之所以有今天的状况，主要归功于英国的坚韧与勤奋、审慎以及组织才能。
英国人同所有其他外国人一样，在这里并非真正意义上的“主人”，他们所取得的有形和无形的成就，并非作为帝国建设者而为之，而被错误地称为“英国”的外人租界绝非大英帝国的一部分。英国人同这里除中国人以外的所有人一样，也只是客人，尽管他们是享有一定契约基础好客待遇的客人。然而，即便是作为客人，他们也为他们的东道主——中国人——完成了大量的工作，简直是奇迹。
法国在印度支那拥有庞大的远东属地。除此之外，她在

big also in the Chinese Republic. We only wish to mention
the French part in the expansion and development of the
Chinese railway system, and the accomplishments for which
French Catholic missions which have created universities,
research institutes and hospitals, are responsible.
Of comparatively more recent date is the
influence of the United States in China. That they practically
refused to accept their share in the Boxer indemnities by
using these amounts for the establishment of schools and
sanitary institutions, inaugurated a new era in the behaviour of
foreigners in China. Hatred and suspicion against foreigners
predominated in China for a long time and only recently the
realisation has gained ground that China can derive large benefits
from occidental culture and occidental economic life.
Through the co-operation between the Chinese
population and the foreigners, the brilliant metropolis of
Shanghai was created, and the power of absorption of which has
proved to be so great that it was able to cope with 20,000
refugees from the Hitler sector of the world in less than 18
months, notwithstanding the fact that war-like conditions
prevail since 1936, although they are not referred-to as war.
It must be remembered that of these refugees - with very few
exceptions - none could find accomedation elsewhere in the world
and that consequently Shanghai was literally a life-saver for
them. Uncounted thousands of us travelled straight from the
concentration camp to the ship which was to take us to the
saving port of Shanghai.
What the total of 20,000 refugees really means,
can be seen from the fact that - with the exception of Russians -
other Europeans and Americans are not much more numerous than
10,000.
The merit of having absorbed in less than 18
months, 20,000 morally hobbled, physically ill-treated,

中华民国的利益也非常巨大。我们仅想提及法国在中国铁路系统的扩张和发展中所起的作用，以及法国天主教传教团在创建大学、研究机构和医院方面所取得的成就。
美国在中国的影响则是相对较近的事情。他们实际上拒绝接受庚子赔款中属于自己的份额，而是将这些款项用于建立学校和卫生机构，这开启了外国人在华行为的新纪元。长期以来，仇外和疑外情绪在中国占主导地位，直到最近，人们才逐渐认识到中国可以从西方文化和西方经济生活中获得巨大利益。
通过中国人口与外国人的合作，造就了辉煌的上海大都市，其吸纳能力被证明是如此之大，以至于尽管自1936年以来战事状态盛行（虽未称之为战争），它仍能在不到18个月的内容纳来自希特勒势力范围内的20,000名难民。
必须记住，这些难民——除极少数例外——在世界其他地方都无法找到容身之所，因此上海对他们来说 literally 是救命稻草。我们中有成千上万的人直接从集中营登上驶往上海这个救命港口的船只。
这20,000名难民的总量究竟意味着什么，从以下事实可见一斑：除俄罗斯人外，其他欧洲人和美国人的总数也不过10,000人左右。
在不到18个月的时间里，吸纳了20,000名在精神上受摧残、身体上受虐待、

page_data.en:
-4-
economically looted Central Europeans, is and will remain a
shining honorary title, a great moral gain which will go down
in the history of the world. In this connection too,
deserved thanks are due to the good-will of the Japanese who
landed troops as a result of hostilities north of the Soochow
Creek and who consequently have a certain executive power in
those parts of the city in which Jewish refugees settled and in
the reconstruction of which they have and still are taking part
to a considerable extent. They have laid no obstacles in their
way, and on the contrary have shown considerable co-operation.
Many of the emigrants who are now in the Far
East, originally desired to emigrate into the great democratic
nations i.e. England, France and the United States. Their
desires were not fulfilled but at least they have come to a
city of international co-operation in which the citizens of
these three great democracies play an important role.
Whoever still doubted that the cause of the
Jews was closely linked to that of democracy must have changed his
mind following the developments which took place in the past
two years.
Two of the already mentioned three States are
at war with Nazi-Germany and anyone whom God has not punished
with hopeless stupidity must have awakened to the fact that the
removal of the swastika-dictatorship in the heart of Europe,
which led to the destruction of personal liberty and the
independence of whole peoples, is desired by the entire human
civilization. Great Britain and France are fighting for liberty,
not only for themselves. The great North-American democracy,
although not at war herself, makes no secret as to where her
page_data.zh:
-4-
经济上被掠夺的中欧难民，这一功绩并将继续作为一项光辉的荣誉头衔，一项巨大的道德收益载入世界史册。在此方面，也应感谢日本人的善意，他们因苏州河以北的敌对行动而派兵登陆，因此在犹太难民定居的城市区域拥有某种行政权力，并在这些区域的重建中已经并正在发挥相当大的作用。他们没有设置障碍，相反表现出了相当的合作。
许多目前身在远东的移民，最初希望移民到伟大的民主国家，即英国、法国和美国。他们的愿望未能实现，但至少他们来到了一座国际合作的城市，而这三个伟大民主国家的公民在其中扮演着重要角色。
任何曾经怀疑犹太人事业与民主事业紧密相连的人，在过去两年发生的事件之后，必定改变了看法。
前述三个国家中的两个正与纳粹德国作战，任何未被上帝惩罚以无可救药的愚蠢之人，都必定已觉醒并认识到，摧毁欧洲中心的卐字独裁统治——该统治导致个人自由和整个民族独立的毁灭——是全人类文明的愿望。英国和法国不仅为自己，也为自由而战。北美伟大的民主国家虽然自身并未参战，但毫不掩饰其

page_data.en:
-5-
sympathies lie, nor of the fact that she considers as enemies
those who preach the Nazi misconception which endangers
everything that is worth living for in life. "Democracy",
said Thomas Mann, the greatest German enemy of the Nazis, when
giving lectures in 15 American cities in 1938, "means well
with human beings. Democracy wishes to uplift them, teach
them and liberate them......its unsocial enemy is called
propaganda. Propaganda is to stupify, level, equalize in the
interests of war-worthiness and particularly, to maintain in
power the dictatorial system."

What we must always repeat to ourselves, we
who were driven out of or voluntarily fled the power-sphere of
the Third Reich to come to Shanghai - and this week there are
again 100 who must repeat this - is that: We must not only be
thankful to destiny that we have escaped the grasp of the Third
Reich, but also for the fact that we have come to a city in the
development of which three great democracies, Great Britain,
France and the United States have had and still have an honorary
part.

We refugees must not interfere with the internal
affairs of the administration of this city, particularly as we
cannot afford to make enemies by taking sides. The other
foreigners - even if there are certain contrasts - are at least
fully empowered citizens of various foreign nations. We on
the other hand only have certain mock documents from our
"home country", Urias letters which are likely to do more harm
and to bring contempt on the owners than to be useful documents.
But also these passports which merely were technical appliances to
facilitate departures, have already for the greater part lost
their validity and in respect to nationality we are bereft not
unlike those whose ship had gone to the bottom of the sea. We
want to live here in peace, work industrially and defy our
calumniators. We want to prove that we can be useful to
general co-operation. In local politics we cannot and should
not indulge.
page_data.zh:
-5-
同情所在，也不掩饰其将那些宣扬纳粹谬误、危及生活中一切值得珍视之物的人视为敌人的事实。“民主”，1938年在15个美国城市发表演讲时，纳粹最大的德国敌人托马斯·曼（Thomas Mann）说道，“意味着对人类怀有善意。民主希望提升他们、教导他们并解放他们……其反社会的敌人叫做宣传。宣传旨在使人愚钝、拉平、均质化，以服务于战备需求，特别是为了维持独裁体制的权力。”

我们这些被迫离开或自愿逃离第三帝国势力范围来到上海的人——本周又有100人必须重复这一点——必须始终对自己重申的是：我们不仅要感谢命运让我们逃脱了第三帝国的魔爪，还要感谢我们来到了一座在其发展过程中，英国、法国和美国这三个伟大民主国家已经并仍在发挥光荣作用的城市。

我们难民不得干涉这座城市行政管理的内部事务，特别是因为我们承担不起因站队而树敌的后果。其他外国人——即使存在某些分歧——至少是各外国的完全授权公民。而我们另一方面，只持有来自我们“祖国”的某些虚假文件，即《乌利亚斯信》（Urias letters，注：指代当时德国犹太人所持的特殊护照或身份证明，常带有歧视性或限制性），这些文件更可能带来伤害并使持有人蒙羞，而非成为有用的证件。但是，这些仅仅作为方便离境的技术性工具的护照，大部分已经失效，就国籍而言，我们如同那些船只沉入海底的人一样一无所有。我们希望在这里和平生活，勤奋工作，驳斥诽谤者。我们要证明我们对普遍合作是有用的。我们不能也不应沉溺于地方政治。

page_data.en:
-6-
There are only three things which no one can
refuse or begrudge us:
(1) That we have that opinion about Nazi Germany -
and we are going to maintain it - which has natural developed
through our experiences and which concur with the opinion held by
all persons of good will on this earth;
(2) That we see our own hopes, joined with those of
the entire liberty-loving humanity, in the three great
democracies, Great Britain, France and the United States, the
pioneers of our own ideals;
(3) And that we know how to value the good fortune
we have in living in a city in the destiny of which citizens of
the three great democracies on earth are co-operating.
page_data.zh:
-6-
只有三件事是任何人都不能拒绝或吝惜给我们的：
(1) 我们对纳粹德国持有那种观点——并且我们将坚持这一观点——这是由我们的经历自然形成的，并与地球上所有善意人士所持的观点一致；
(2) 我们将自己的希望与全人类热爱自由的希望一起，寄托在三个伟大民主国家——英国、法国和美国身上，它们是我们理想的先驱；
(3) 我们知道如何珍惜我们的幸运，即生活在一座其命运中有地球上三个伟大民主国家公民共同参与合作的城市里。

CHINA PRESS.
MAY 3 1939
05615
REGISTRY
D. 849 F62

New German Magazine Makes
Its Appearance In Shanghai

Another new magazine made its
appearance in Shanghai yesterday.
This one is the "Gelbe Post," a bi-
monthly publication in the German
language edited by Mr. A. J. Stor-
fer, emigre from Austria.

Mr. Storfer was a co-worker of
the great psychoanalyst, Dr. S.
Freud. He published the doctor's
magazines and assisted in the
publication and editing of Freud's
books.

The fact that Mr. Storfer knows
his business is vividly revealed in
the first issue of the "Gelbe Post."
It is not only filled with timely
reading material of interest to the
large Jewish refugee population in
Shanghai but it is one of the best
printed and edited periodicals to
make its appearance in this city
in years.

One of the major articles in the
first issue of the magazine is about
Yunnan Province. It was written
by Dr. Bruno Kroper with the idea
of informing Jewish refugees about
West China.

West China, at the present time,
means something to the majority
of Jewish refugees in Shanghai
since the Chinese National Govern-
ment is giving serious thought to
the Settlement of refugees in that
part of the country, especially the
Yunnan area.

Other articles in the first issue
of "Gelbe Post," include studies of
the progress made in psychoanalysis
in Japan and China, an article on
Madame Chiang Kai-shek and the
New Life Movement and a study
of the Chinese Jew. Taken on the
whole, "Gelbe Post" is an excellent
piece of editorial and printing
work.—C.D.A.

D. 849 F62

新德文杂志在上海问世

昨天，又一本新杂志在上海问世。
这本杂志名为《黄色邮报》（Gelbe Post），是一份德文双月刊，由奥地利流亡者 A. J. 斯托弗（A. J. Storfer）先生编辑。

斯托弗先生曾是伟大的精神分析学家 S. 弗洛伊德博士的同事。他出版了这位博士的杂志，并协助出版和编辑弗洛伊德的著作。

斯托弗先生精通此道的事实，在《黄色邮报》的创刊号中得到了生动体现。该刊不仅刊登了大量对上海庞大的犹太难民群体具有吸引力的时事阅读材料，而且是近年来在该市出现的印刷和编辑质量最好的期刊之一。

该杂志创刊号的主要文章之一是关于云南省的。该文由布鲁诺·克罗珀（Bruno Kroper）博士撰写，旨在向犹太难民介绍中国西部。

目前，中国西部对上海大多数犹太难民来说具有重要意义，因为中国政府正认真考虑在该地区，特别是云南地区安置难民。

《黄色邮报》创刊号的其他文章包括对日本和中国精神分析学进展的研究、一篇关于蒋介石夫人和新生活运动的文章，以及对中国犹太人的研究。总体而言，《黄色邮报》是一部优秀的编辑和印刷作品。——C.D.A.

Date May 6, 1939）

Subject Observation re the "Yellow Post"

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

Perusal of the attached first issue of
"Gelbe (Yellow) Post" which is owned, edited and
published by Mr. A.J. Storfer, an emigrant from Germany,
indicates that the aim of the paper is not to further
the Zionist cause in the Far East but rather to serve
as a periodical aiming at enlightening, in the first
place, other German Jewish new arrivals about the
conditions in the Far East and the countries surrounding
the Pacific in general.

Special importance is laid in the first
issue to an article entitled "Yunnan - the Country of
the Future" which aims at calling the attention of
Jewish emigrants to the Province of Yunnan as a country
of great possibilities for them. Other topics discussed
are articles about Tsingtao, Leprosy and Superstition,
Land prices and rents in Shanghai, the Jews of Kaifengfu
and kindred subjects of local interest. A special
feature of the periodical will be articles on "Psycho-
analyses" in which subject the editor, Mr. A.J. Storfer,
is an expert of high order, having formerly published
several international periodicals on Psycho-analyses
in Vienna.

In the introduction of his periodical to the
public, Mr. A.J. Storfer states that his paper will
engage on reporting political events, though purely
informatively, without taking sides or being tendencious
in order to insure the neutral character of his paper.

With a view to explaining to him the local
situation and the stand of the Municipal Council in
regard to local publications, Mr. A.J. Storfer, followi

主题：关于《黄色邮报》的观察报告

由帕普（Papp）督察制作并提交。

经审阅附上的《Gelbe (Yellow) Post》（黄色邮报）创刊号，该刊物由德国移民 A.J. 斯托弗先生所有、编辑和出版，表明该报的目的并非在远东推进犹太复国主义事业，而是旨在作为一种期刊，首先向其他新抵达的德籍犹太人阐明远东及环太平洋国家的一般情况。

创刊号特别重视一篇题为“云南——未来之国”的文章，旨在引起犹太移民对云南省的关注，将其视为充满巨大机遇的地方。其他讨论的话题包括关于青岛、麻风病与迷信、上海的地价与租金、开封府的犹太人以及其他具有地方兴趣的相关主题。该期刊的一个特色栏目将是关于“精神分析”的文章，编辑 A.J. 斯托弗先生在此领域是一位高阶专家，此前曾在维也纳出版过数种关于精神分析的国际期刊。

在向公众介绍其期刊时，A.J. 斯托弗先生声明，他的报纸将报道政治事件，但纯粹以提供信息为目的，不偏袒任何一方，也不带倾向性，以确保其中立性质。

THE INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR THE
ORGANIZATION OF EUROPEAN IMMIGRANTS
IN CHINA

SHANGHAI, 19th September 1940.

PK/Fa.    To the Commissioner
          Shanghai Municipal Police,
          SHANGHAI.

Dear Sir,

          Recently an Emigrant German language newspaper,
the "Gelbe Post", was acquired by its senior contempor-
ary, the "Shanghai Jewish Chronicle", and thereby a life
and death struggle between two competitors was terminated
much to the relief of all concerned, including this Com-
mittee which was, time and again, called upon to try to
effect an understanding or working agreement between two
rival publications.

          In this connection I was called upon to arbitrate,
adjust, smooth out, persuade etc. etc. in numerous inter-
views singly and jointly with the proprietors of the two
papers and I must confess that the task was not a pleasant
one.

          It was quite evident that the two papers could not
exist and that both were losing heavily. A continuance of
the feude would have meant the suspension of both papers
with the resultant loss of work for about 25o Emigrants
or more, who were earning their living in connection with
the two publications.

          The taking over of the "Gelbe Post" was, therefore,
a happy solution which entailed certain immediate sacri-
fices for the owner of the "Shanghai Jewish Chronicle",
but which he hopes to recoup gradually in the course of
time.

          Hardly has, however, this happy solution been
brought about, when it is reported to me that application
has been made to you for the licensing of a new Emigrant
German language paper. This enterprise is, I am told, to
be financed by the English wife of a German Emigrant and
amongst others a Mr. Horst Lewin and a Mr. Wolff are in-
terested for personal reasons, to get the paper started
and to make out of it what they can whilst the going is
good.

          In the interest of all concerned, I am strongly
of the opinion that there is no justification for the pub-
lication of such a paper as it would, by no means, fill
a public need or even an Emigrant need. The two papers
now published, one in the morning and the other in the
evening, are ample for all purposes and a new competitor
would only mean a new paper war, doing no one any good
and a lot of harm possibly to many.

          I have also been informed that the proposed paper's
policy was to be one "agin' the government" i.e. black-
                                                          ./.

（印：SHANGHAI 21 SEPT. 1940 COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）

在华欧洲移民组织国际委员会

上海，1940年9月19日。

PK/Fa.    致警务处长
          上海公共租界工部局警务处，
          上海。

尊敬的先生：

          最近，一份德文移民报纸《黄色邮报》被其资历较老的同行《上海犹太纪事报》收购，从而终止了两家竞争对手之间生死攸关的斗争，令所有相关方深感欣慰，其中包括本委员会，该委员会曾多次被要求试图在两家 rival 出版物之间达成谅解或工作协议。

          在这方面，我被要求在与两家报纸的所有者单独或共同进行的多次会谈中进行仲裁、调解、缓和、劝说等，我必须承认，这项任务并不令人愉快。

          很明显，这两家报纸无法共存，且两者都在遭受严重亏损。如果争斗继续下去，将意味着两家报纸均停刊，从而导致大约250名或更多依靠这两家出版物谋生的移民失业。

          因此，收购《黄色邮报》是一个令人满意的解决方案，虽然这给《上海犹太纪事报》的所有者带来了一些即时的牺牲，但他希望随着时间的推移逐渐收回成本。

          然而，这一令人满意的解决方案刚刚达成，我就接到报告称，有人向您申请许可创办一份新的德文移民报纸。据告知，该企业将由一位德国移民的英国妻子资助，此外，霍斯特·莱温（Horst Lewin）先生和沃尔夫（Wolff）先生等人出于个人原因，有兴趣启动该报纸，并在形势有利时从中获利。

          为了所有相关方的利益，我强烈认为，出版此类报纸是没有正当理由的，因为它绝不会满足公众需求，甚至无法满足移民需求。目前出版的两份报纸，一份在上午，另一份在晚上，已足以满足所有目的，新的竞争对手只会意味着新一轮的报纸战争，这对任何人都没有好处，反而可能对许多人造成大量伤害。

          我还获悉，拟议报纸的政策将是“反对政府”，即抹黑
                                                          ./.

（印：上海 1940年9月21日 警务处长办公室）

Subject Shanghai Jewish Chronicle - Gelbe Post - Reported amalgamation

Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

On 20.9.40 a letter was received from Mr. Paul
Komor, Hon. Sec. of the International Committee for the
Organization of European Immigrants in China to the
effect that the Gelbe Post had been acquired by the
Shanghai Jewish Chronicle. The writer goes on to
say that there is no room for more than one local
immigrant morning paper and adds that he has now heard
that an application has been made to this office by
Mr. Horst Lewin, Mr. Wolff and the English wife of
a German Immigrant for re-registration of the Gelbe
Post.

So far as this office is aware the present
position and history of the two papers is as follows:-
Shanghai Jewish Chronicle was first registered
with S.M. Police in the name of Mr. Osias Lewin as
Editor, Publisher and Proprietor and Registration
Certificate issued on 26.4.39.

Gelbe Post was first registered in the name of
Adolf Josef Storfer, Editor, Publisher and Proprietor
on 17.3.39 as a semi-monthly, was changed to a bi-
weekly in January 1940 and to a daily in February 1940.

On 30.8.40 a letter was received from
Mr. Storfer to the effect that he had sold all his
rights in the publication to Osias Lewin and a similar
letter from Mr. Lewin stating he had purchased the
paper.

On September 3, 1940, Mr. O. Lewin called at
this office and made application for re-registration

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JUN 19 1939

Feting

OSSI LEWIN

Jewish Chronicle
Makes Progress

Paper Celebrates 50th
Issue, Serves Big
Refugee Colony

Celebrating its 50th day of issue
as a morning newspaper, the
Shanghai Jewish Chronicle, only
local news organ published by
and for Jews, will jump from six
to eight pages of contents, news,
views and features Sunday.

It was 50 days ago that this
newspaper, published in both the
German and English languages,
put on the streets its first issue.
Only 1000 copies were printed as
the weekly Shanghai Jewish
Chronicle's editor waited anxiously
to see the results of his adventure
into the daily newspaper field.

Rapid Progress
Since that day, the Chronicle
has recorded phenomenal pro-
gress and its circulation is now at
the 3000 mark with increases the
daily rule rather than the excep-
tion. Utilizing the foreign news
agencies, and employing an ex-
perienced staff to cover local
events, the newspaper gives its
readers full coverage of world and
Shanghai happenings.

It plays an especial role in the
local press world for it made its
appearance at a critical moment
in the fortunes of some 15,000
Jewish refugees who have found
new homes in Shanghai. It is
read by the whole of this huge
community, passing from hand to
hand, and in addition goes to the
homes of the many foreign Jews
already long established here.

Wide Experience
It enters a field as yet mainly
left untouched by local journalism
and as such is a pioneer. Its
editor, Mr. Ossi Lewin, is said
to be particularly suited to his
job, for he himself is also a
pioneer in many respects.

Still a young man, he has had
wide experience in journalism and
arrived in Shanghai less than a
year ago, correspondent of the
Jewish Telegraph Agency Limited,
London.

Native Of Vienna
Native of Vienna, he was well
known in Austria as a prominent
member of Zionist organizations
and newspaper and magazine
publications. On his arrival in
Shanghai, after serving as cor-
respondent in Italy during 1937,
he resumed his Zionist activities.
He soon came to enjoy the
esteem of his colleagues in Zionist
fields of endeavor and was ap-
pointed a member of the presi-
dium of the "Kadimah," local
branch of the Jewish Agency of
which Mr. Touro is the President.
His educational activities and his
work in connection with the weekly
Chronicle have been marked by
such energy and devotion that the
newspaper has become an estab-
lished institution.

FILE

费廷（Feting）

奥西·莱温（OSSI LEWIN）

《犹太纪事报》
取得进展

报纸庆祝第50期发行，服务大型难民社区

《上海犹太纪事报》作为唯一由犹太人创办并面向犹太人的本地新闻机构，在庆祝其作为晨报发行的第50天之际，将于周日将内容、新闻、观点和特写的版面从六版增至八版。

就在50天前，这份以德文和英文出版的报纸发出了第一期。当时仅印刷了1000份，因为这份周报《上海犹太纪事报》的编辑焦急地等待着他进军日报领域的成果。

迅速进展
自那天起，《纪事报》取得了惊人的进展，其发行量现在达到3000份，且每日增长已成为常态而非例外。利用外国通讯社，并雇用经验丰富的员工报道本地事件，该报为其读者提供世界和上海发生的事件的全面报道。

它在本地新闻界扮演着特殊的角色，因为它出现在大约15,000名在上海找到新家的犹太难民命运的关键时刻。这个庞大社区的所有人都阅读该报，它被传阅，此外还送到许多早已在此定居的外国犹太人的家中。

广泛经验
它进入了一个尚未被本地新闻业主要触及的领域，因此是先行者。据说其编辑奥西·莱温（Ossi Lewin）先生特别适合这项工作，因为他本人在许多方面也是先行者。

虽然仍年轻，他在新闻业方面有着广泛的经验，不到一年前抵达上海，担任伦敦犹太电讯社有限公司（Jewish Telegraph Agency Limited）的通讯员。

维也纳人
作为维也纳人，他在奥地利作为犹太复国主义组织的知名成员以及报纸和杂志出版人而闻名。在1937年担任意大利通讯员后抵达上海时，他恢复了犹太复国主义活动。他很快赢得了犹太复国主义领域同事的尊重，并被任命为“卡迪玛”（Kadimah，即当地犹太代办处分支，由图罗（Touro）先生任主席）主席团成员。他的教育活动以及他与周刊《纪事报》相关的工作充满了活力和奉献精神，使得该报已成为一个稳固的机构。

page_data.en:
Contents of the newspaper :

1) Local and general news , usually in form of a weekly review . The
tendency shall be non-political and the material may be taken from
the daily papers or obtained through the big agencies, i.e.Reuter,
United Press, etc.

2) A certain amount of space is to be devoted to the interests of the
refugees in Shanghai, in co-operation with the relief committee.

3) xxxxxxxxxx News , circulars, advertisements etc. from the committees
will be published, especially offers pertaining to jobs.

4) The economic possibilities for refugees both in Shanghai and in the
interior of China will be discussed.

5) The possibilities for re-emigration from Shanghai will be examined.

6) Conditions in Shanghai , as regards law, administration, etc.
will be examined. Some general advice will be given regarding life
here, in co-operation with the committee.

7) There will be articles by JTA , London regarding countries which
offer a chance to Jewish immigrants, notably Palestine .

8) Some space will be devoted to features and humour.

9) There will be space alternatingly devoted to hygiene, sports, letters
to the editor, etc.

Tendency:

In the first place, the Jewish interests in Shanghai are to be
considered. As regards Germany, an attitude of strict self-censorship is
adopted, i.e. there will be no news and articles regarding Germany.
We shall do our best to promote the education of the Jewish masses
which are at present lacking in discipline . Their adaptation to the
new environment shall be promoted.
page_data.zh:
报纸内容：

1) 本地及一般新闻，通常以每周综述的形式呈现。倾向应为非政治性，材料可取自日报或通过大型通讯社获取，即路透社、合众社等。

2) 将与救济委员会合作，留出一定版面关注上海难民的利益。

3) 将刊登各委员会的新闻、通告、广告等，特别是与求职相关的信息。

4) 将探讨难民在上海及中国内地的经济前景。

5) 将考察从上海再移民的可能性。

6) 将考察上海在法律、行政等方面的状况。将与委员会合作，就在此地生活提供一般性建议。

7) 将刊登伦敦犹太电讯社（JTA）关于为犹太移民提供机会的国家（特别是巴勒斯坦）的文章。

8) 将留出部分版面刊登特写和幽默作品。

9) 将交替留出版面刊登卫生、体育、读者来信等内容。

倾向：

首先，要考虑在沪犹太人的利益。关于德国，采取严格自我审查的态度，即不刊登有关德国的新闻和文章。我们将尽力促进目前缺乏纪律的犹太大众的教育。我们将促进他们适应新环境。

SUBJECT: Re letter received from Jewish Chronicle.

On the 24-2-43 a letter was received by this
office, to the effect that the Jewish Chronicle applies
for permission for the publication of Advertisements
from Refugees within the designated area for the
letting of Apartments or houses etc. The argument
brought forward by the said Newspaper is that some
persons are entirely at the mercy of Agents and their
scrupulees machinations, They furthermore states
that should such people be able to advertise in the
local Newspaper, they would not need to utilise Agents.

Here the undersigned wishes to point out that
should the instructions re the advertisement be lifted,
unauthorised persons would than advertise and obtain

The undersigned respectfully suggests, that this

of 70 Muirhead Road is dealing with the exchange of

fore anyone wishing to lease any part of the premises,

Translation of an Article in the Shanghai
Jewish Chronicle of Febr. 25th, 1943, written
by the Editor, Osias Lewin.

Endeavours and Understanding towards the
Execution of the Proclamation.

The manifold changes, by which the fate of every nation
is accompanied in this, the greatest of all struggles, have also
brought about a new turn for our community and have struck it hard.
In this serious hour we face the new situation with a sense of reality
and we shall mobilize all our forces in order to secure our existence
on a modest scale in the light of the newly created situation. In
this manner only we can secure a future possibility of existence if
the authorities grant us their generosity and understanding.

It gives us consolation that this can be expected with
considerable certainty. The writer of these lines was given the oppor-
tunity to gain this impression during a long interview with the compe-
tent representative of the authorities, Mr. Kubota, who has been charged
with the execution of the proclamation.

My visit to the "Office for Shanghai Stateless Refugee
Affairs" has impressed me deeply. There a very friendly atmosphere pre-
vails and every single applicant can observe the good will of the
officials, working there, who are trying their best to give the best
advice possible to the hundreds of daily callers, and to impart the
necessary information to them.

Immediately on entering the office I meet Mr. Ghoya, who
discharges his functions here. In the room people are pressing, they
are surrounding Mr. Ghoya in a demi-circle who, pointing at a map, gives
them information. In his fluent English he tries to impart to the
enquirers the desired knowledge, but he has to repeat his words fre-
quently, due to the deficient knowledge of the English language of most
of the Emigrants, until they leave in grateful acknowledgement of the
information received. The observer is surprised at the amount of pa-
tience with which the official carries out his duty, there is no trace
of formality or automatic execution of duty. One feels that that human
feeling and understanding are extended to the caller here.

FILE
