1943年2月27日

1943年2月25日《上海犹太纪事报》上一篇文章的译文，由编辑奥西亚斯·莱温（Osias Lewin）撰写。

努力与理解以执行公告。

在这场所有斗争中最大的斗争中，伴随每个民族命运的多重变化，也给我们社区带来了新的转折，并给予了沉重打击。在这严峻时刻，我们以现实感面对新局面，并将动员我们所有的力量，以便在新形成的局势下，以 modest scale（适度的规模）确保我们的生存。只有以这种方式，如果当局给予我们慷慨和理解，我们才能确保未来的生存可能性。

令人欣慰的是，这在很大程度上是可以预期的。本文作者有机会在与负责执行公告的主管当局代表久保田（Kubota）先生的一次长时间会谈中获得了这一印象。

我对“上海无国籍难民事务办公室”的访问给我留下了深刻印象。那里洋溢着非常友好的气氛，每一位申请者都能观察到在那里工作的官员们的善意，他们正尽最大努力为每天数百名来访者提供尽可能好的建议，并向他们提供必要的信息。

一进办公室，我就遇到了在此履行职责的戈亚（Ghoya）先生。房间里挤满了人，他们半圆形地围在戈亚先生周围，他指着地图向他们提供信息。他用流利的英语试图向询问者传授所需的知识，但由于大多数移民英语水平有限，他不得不频繁重复他的话，直到他们带着对所得信息的感激之情离开。观察者对该官员履行职责时的耐心程度感到惊讶，没有丝毫的形式主义或机械执行任务的痕迹。人们感觉到，这里向来访者伸出了人情味和理解之手。

FILE

page_data.en:
-2-

After a short while I am sitting opposite Mr. Kubota,
the directing brain. Simple, serious, and with great understanding,
Mr. Kubota dicusses all questions whichIp t,relating to the Proclamation
wit reference to the interests of our community. All our problems are
known to Mr.Kubota and he discu..es them extensively. Prepuations are
being made and detailed regulations will be promulgated in order to
prevent private unscrupulous activities,e.g. in housing matters and to
carry through everything in a considerate and orderly manner. With
particular emphasis Mr. Kubota stresses that the proclamation is due
only to military necessity and that there is absolutely no antisemitic
motive at the bottom of it. On the contrary, he emphasizes, that every
antisemitic tendency in Shanghai will be suppressed with full force and
going further, he will even care for the securing of work. It is also
his desire to further our organizations in every way. Public buildings
within the district as well as vacant lots for buildings may also be
alloted. On big map, XXXXXXXX, on which the Emigrants' district is
marked, Mr.Kubota shows me the demarkation line. He points at three
different points lying outside XXX the district: "Ort","S.J.Y.A."school,
Wayside Camp. For all three,permission was granted for continuation, free-
dom of movement will also be maintained.

About all these matters and many others Mr.Kubota talks
in his serious and engaging manner and one leaves him with the pleasant
feeling that the fate of our community has been put into the hands of
a man, who has treated our numerous problems with so great understanding
and who has in this manner given proof of a readiness to help, which will
secure for him the particular gratitude of our great community.

The "Shanghai Jewish Chronicle"will endeavour, in contact
with this office, to give the greatest possible space in its columns to
facts relating to the above, in order to exclude rumours right from the
beginning.
page_data.zh:
-2-

过了一会儿，我坐在主导人物久保田先生的对面。久保田先生朴实、严肃且极具理解力，讨论了就公告而言与我们社区利益相关的所有问题。久保田先生了解我们所有的问题，并进行了广泛的讨论。正在制定准备工作，并将颁布详细规定，以防止私人的无耻活动，例如在住房事务方面，并以体贴和有序的方式贯彻一切。久保田先生特别强调，公告仅出于军事必要，其背后绝对没有反犹动机。相反，他强调，上海的任何反犹倾向都将受到全力压制，进而，他甚至将关心就业保障。他也希望以各种方式促进我们的组织发展。区内的公共建筑以及用于建筑的空地也可分配。在一张标有移民区的大地图 XXXXXXXX 上，久保田先生向我展示了分界线。他指向位于 XXX 区外的三个不同地点：“Ort”、“S.J.Y.A.”学校、路边营地（Wayside Camp）。这三个地方均获准继续存在，行动自由也将得以维持。

久保田先生以其严肃而引人入胜的方式谈论了所有这些事项及许多其他事项，离开他时，人们怀着愉快的感觉，认为我们社区的命运已掌握在一个如此富有理解力地对待我们众多问题的人手中，他以这种方式证明了乐于助人的意愿，这将为我们广大社区赢得特别的感激。

《上海犹太纪事报》将与该办公室保持联系，在其版面上尽可能多地刊登与上述内容相关的事实，以便从一开始就排除谣言。

DONNERSTAG, 25. FEBRUAR 1943
SHANGHAI JEWISH CHRONICLE

Bemuehungen und Verstaendnis zur praktischen
Durchfuehrung der Proklamation

Die mannigfaltigen Veraenderungen, die das Schick-
sal einer jeden Nation in diesem groessten Voelkerringen
mit sich bringt, hat auch fuer unsere Gemeinschaft eine
neue Wendung gebracht und sie hart betroffen. Wir
stehen in dieser ernsten Stunde mit realem Sinn der
neuen Situation gegenueber und werden alle unsere
Kraefte mobil machen, um der neu geschaffenen Lage
im bescheidenen Rahmen unserer Existenz gerecht zu
werden, was unter den gegebenen Umstanden nur
dann unsere kuenftige Lebensmoeglichkeit sichern kann,
wenn die Behoerden uns ihr hochherziges Entgegenkom-
men und Verstaendnis zuteil werden lassen.
Und gerade das Letztere darf zu unserem Trost in
dieser schwierigen Lage mit ziemlicher Sicherheit vor-
ausgesetzt werden. Der Schreiber dieser Zeilen hatte
Gelegenheit, diesen Eindruck waehrend eines laengeren
Gespraechs mit dem zustaendigen Repraesentanten der
Behoerden, Mr. Kubota, der beauftragt ist, die Ver-
wirklichung der Proklamation durchzufuehren, zu ge-
winnen.
Mein Besuch in dem fuer die Durchfuehrung der
Proklamation zustaendigen Buero hat auf mich den
nachhaltigsten Eindruck hinterlassen. Es herrscht dort
eine absolut freundliche Atmosphaere und jeder einzelne
Applikant kann den guten Willen der diensthabenden
Beamten feststellen, die in jeder Weise bemueht sind,
die grosse Zahl der hier taeglich zu Hunderten vor-
sprechenden Menschen mit dem groessten Verstaendnis
zu beraten und ihnen die noetigen Auskuenfte zu er-
teilen.
Gleich beim Betreten des Bueross stosse ich auf Mr.
Ghoya, der hier seines Amtes waltet. Im Zimmer herrscht
ein grosser Andrang die Leute stehen im Halbkreis um
Mr. Ghoya herum, der ihnen, auf eine Karte deutend,
Auskunft erteilt. Mit seinem fliessenden Englisch versucht
er den Auskunftbegehrenden die gewuenschten Infor-
mationen zu vermitteln, muss jedoch den meisten Emi-
granten mit Ruecksicht auf ihre mangelhafte Kenntnis
der englischen Sprache die Auskunft oeffter wiederholen,
um sich die Betreffenden in Kenntnis der Dinge denken
koennen. Der Beobachter bewundert, mit welcher
Geduld der Beamte seinen Dienst versieht, keine Spur
von Ueberdruss oder momentaner Pflichterfuellung
zeigt sich in seiner Miene, und das Ver-

Nach kurzer Zeit sitze ich der leitenden Hand, Mr.
Kubota, gegenueber. Einfach und ernst und mit grossem
Verstaendnis diskutiert Mr. Kubota alle Fragen, die ich
im Interesse unserer Gemeinschaft im Zusammenhang
mit der Proklamation aufwerfe. Alle unsere Probleme
sind Mr. Kubota bekannt und er diskutiert sie aus-
fuehrlich. Es werden Vorbereitungen getroffen und
Detailbestimmungen so abgefasst werden, um eine private
und skrupellose Betaetigung wie zum Beispiel auf dem
Gebiete des Wohnproblems zu unterbinden und alles
milde und in geregelter Form durchzufuehren. Mr.
Kubota weist mit besonderem Nachdruck darauf hin,
dass die Proklamation lediglich eine militaerische Not-
wendigkeit sei, und ihr gar kein antisemitisches Motiv zu
Grunde liegt. Im Gegenteil, er betont sogar, dass jede
antisemitische Regung in Shanghai auf das Staerkste
unterdrueckt werden wird und will darueber hinaus fuer
Arbeitsbeschaffung Sorge tragen. Er wuenscht auch in
jeder Weise unsere Organisationen zu foerdern. Oeffent-
liche Gebaeude, die im Distrikt liegen, sowie Baugrund
sollen eventuell gleichfalls zur Verfuegung gestellt wer-
den. Auf einer grossen Karte, auf der der Emigranten-
Distrikt eingezeichnet ist, zeigt mir Mr. Kubota die
Markierungslinie. Er deutet auf drei Punkte, die in den
verschiedensten Gegenden ausserhalb des Distriktes lie-
gen: ORT, S.J.Y.A.-School, Wayside-Heim. Fuer alle
drei wurde die Erlaubnis fuer den Weiterverbleib erteilt,
ebenso wird die Bewegungsfreiheit aufrecht erhalten
bleiben.
Ueber all diese Dinge und vieles andere diskutieren
Mr. Kubota in seiner ernsten und liebenswuerdigen Art
und man verlaesst ihn mit dem angenehmen Gefuehl,
dass das Schicksal unserer Gemeinschaft in die Haende
eines Menschen gelegt wurde, der unsere zahlreichen
Probleme mit so grossem Verstaendnis behandelt, und auf
diese Weise eine Hilfsbereitschaft dokumentiert, die ihm
die besondere Dankbarkeit unserer gesamten Gemeinde
sichert.

1943年2月25日，星期四
《上海犹太纪事报》

为切实执行公告所作的努力与理解

在这个最大的民族斗争中，每个国家的命运都伴随着各种各样的变化，这也给我们社区带来了新的转折，并使我们受到沉重打击。在这严峻的时刻，我们以现实的态度面对新形势，并将动员我们所有的力量，在我们生存的有限范围内适应新造成的局面。只有在当局给予我们慷慨的通融和理解的情况下，这才能确保我们在给定环境下的未来生存可能性。

而在目前的困难局势下，我们可以相当有把握地假定，后者正是我们的慰藉所在。本文作者有机会在与负责执行该公告的当局代表久保田先生（Mr. Kubota）进行长时间谈话期间，获得了这一印象。

我对负责执行公告的办公室的访问给我留下了最深刻的印象。那里的气氛绝对友好，每一位申请者都能感受到值班官员的善意，他们竭力以最大的理解力，为每天数百名前来咨询的人提供建议并给予必要的信息。

我一进入办公室就遇到了在此任职的戈亚先生（Mr. Ghoya）。房间里拥挤不堪，人们半圆形地围在戈亚先生周围，他指着地图向他们提供信息。他用流利的英语试图向寻求信息者传达所需的信息，但由于大多数移民英语水平有限，他不得不多次重复回答，以便让他们了解情况。观察者钦佩这位官员服务时的耐心，他的脸上没有流露出丝毫的厌倦或仅仅是履行职责的神情，而那种——

不久后，我坐在负责人久保田先生对面。久保田先生朴实、严肃且充满理解地讨论了我为了我们社区的利益而提出的与公告有关的所有问题。久保田先生熟悉我们所有的问题，并进行了详细讨论。目前正在采取准备工作，并起草细则，以制止私人及无良行为，例如在住房问题上的此类行为，并以温和且规范的形式执行一切。久保田先生特别强调指出，该公告仅仅是一种军事必要，其背后没有任何反犹动机。相反，他甚至强调，上海的任何反犹情绪都将受到最严厉的镇压，并且他还打算设法提供就业机会。他也希望在各方面促进我们的组织发展。位于该区内的公共建筑以及建筑用地也可能被提供使用。在一张标有移民区的地图上，久保田先生向我展示了界线。他指出了位于该区外不同地方的三个点：ORT、S.J.Y.A.学校、韦赛德之家（Wayside-Heim）。这三个地方都已获准继续留驻，行动自由也将得以维持。

久保田先生以其严肃而亲切的方式讨论了所有这些事情及许多其他事项，人们离开时带着一种愉快的感觉，即我们社区的命运掌握在一个如此充满理解地处理我们众多问题的人手中，从而展现了一种乐于助人的态度，这为我们整个社区赢得了对他特别的感激之情。

SHANGHAI, November 24th, 1941

Shanghai Municipal Police
Police-Headquarters
185. Foochow Road
L O C A L

Dear Sirs,

we hereby beg to bring to your knowledge an incident which occurred during the printing of our latest Sunday-issue in the Saturday night.

Our latest Sunday-issue comprised 24 pages. We had made all preparations to ensure the punctual appearance of the paper. Sufficient copies were set in time , so that we were able to print four pages already on Saturday afternoon.

In the beginning of the night five Linotype-machines were operated for our paper and the whole work progressed like usual, so that we could hope to issue the paper punctually inspite of its greater size.

At about 2 o'clock a.m. printer No.1 appeared in the correction-room and announced that the printers are disappeared, except one and his assistant. He stated that under these circumstances only one machine were to be operated , so that every printing-form (four pages) had to wait for the previous form to be finished in print. He urged us to speed up our work.

Some time later one form could already be given into the printing-machine. The next form could, however, not more be printed even with this one machine, since also the last printer was gone. We were, therefore, forced to wait for the printers of the day-shift, so that the Sunday-paper could be published at length about noon.

In the Mercury Press I was to-day assured that the paper can be published to-morrow as usually, since new printers have been engaged.

A young member of my editorial-department who resides in the Jewish refugee-camp Chaouffong Road, where also Mr.Rolf David is living, informed us this morning that he met Mr.David this morning, when the latter returned from his night-work at "Shanghaier Morgenpost". Mr.David asked smiling our employee, Mr.Manfred Kochmann, by what reasons our Sunday-edition had been so late. When he got no answer, he added: "How does it happen that the printers of "Jewish Chronicle" come to us?" - We beg to enclose the respective statement, undersigned by Mr.Manfred Kochmann.

警察总局

本地

尊敬的先生们：

我们谨此提请贵方注意一起事件，该事件发生在上周六夜间印刷我们最新一期周日版报纸期间。

我们最新的周日版共有24页。我们已做好所有准备，以确保报纸准时出版。足够的版面已及时排好，因此我们能够在周六下午已经印刷了四页。

夜幕开始时，五台莱诺铸排机（Linotype-machines）为我们的报纸运作，整个工作像往常一样进展，因此尽管版面较大，我们仍有希望准时出报。

大约在凌晨2点，1号印刷工出现在校对室，宣布除了他和他的助手外，其他印刷工都消失了。他表示，在这种情况下，只能运行一台机器，因此每个印版（四页）都必须等待前一个印版印刷完成。他催促我们加快工作速度。

过了一会儿，一个印版已经可以送入印刷机。然而，即使是这一台机器也无法再印刷下一个印版，因为最后一名印刷工也离开了。因此，我们被迫等待白班印刷工到来，导致周日报纸直到中午左右才得以出版。

今天在水星印刷厂，有人向我保证，由于已雇佣了新印刷工，报纸明天可以照常出版。

我编辑部的一名年轻成员居住在兆丰路（Chaouffong Road）的犹太难民营，罗尔夫·大卫先生（Mr. Rolf David）也住在那里。他今天早上通知我们，他在罗尔夫·大卫先生从《上海晨报》（Shanghaier Morgenpost）夜班工作回来时遇见了他。大卫先生微笑着询问我们的员工曼弗雷德·科赫曼先生（Mr. Manfred Kochmann），为什么我们的周日版出版得这么晚。当没有得到回答时，他补充道：“《犹太纪事报》的印刷工怎么会到我们这里来？”——我们谨附上由曼弗雷德·科赫曼先生签署的相关陈述。

此致
敬礼

《上海犹太纪事报》出版人

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室）

Mr. Manfred Kochmann makes this morning the following
statement:
"Yesterday evening at about 9 o'clock I met Mr. Rolf David in
our refugee-camp and asked him, how many workmen had been lured from
away from Mercury Press. Mr. David declared thereupon , so far as he
knows, three workers until now, but many of them would still follow,
as Mr. Selmanson deals with this matter."
Manfred Kochmann
We want to remark in this connection that Mr. Ephraim Selmanson
has been with our paper since its foundation until the foundation of
the "Shanghaiier Morgenpost". He was a member of our night-staff and
was therefore in permanent connection with the night-staff of the
Mercury Press.

"Nedelia" dated 19-8-39. Publisher and editor - Mr. M.A.Galkin,
House 17,125 Route de Grouchy.

OUR AIMS.

..."In the conflicts which are imminent both in the West and
here in the East we,Russians, shall not be able to keep out of
events,but taking full consideration of these events must decide
upon and follow our own course."...

..." We firmly bear in mind that we are guests of our east-
ern neighbours - China and Japan,guests of foreign concessions
and we consider that,being people who refused to recognize the re-
gime of slavery in Russia,we must strictly abide by law and order
here, so that we might facilitate the prosperity of Russians in
the same way as our hosts facilitate their own prosperity"

By our productive and useful work we must earn the re-
spect and recognition of our hosts as a necessary economic factor
in the development of countries of Eastern Asia and to prepare the
path for the future Russian commerce and industry in the Far East!

..." In starting our activities we appeal to Russian
residents in the Far East to work hard for their own welfare as
well as for the common welfare of all Russians and,forgetting
their internal discords to unify in strong organizations built up
on healthy foundations and purely business principles".

我们的目标。

……“在西方和东方即将发生的冲突中，我们俄罗斯人将无法置身事外，但在充分考虑这些事件的同时，必须决定并遵循我们自己的道路。”……

……“我们 firmly 牢记，我们是我们的东方邻居——中国和日本的客人，是外国租界的客人，我们认为，作为拒绝承认俄罗斯奴隶制度的人，我们必须在这里严格遵守法律和秩序，以便像东道主促进自身繁荣一样，促进俄罗斯人的繁荣”

通过我们富有成效和有益的工作，我们必须赢得东道主的尊重和认可，成为东亚国家发展中必要的经济因素，并为未来俄罗斯在远东的商业和工业铺平道路！

……“在开始我们的活动时，我们呼吁远东的俄罗斯居民为自己的福利以及所有俄罗斯人的共同福利而努力工作，忘记内部纷争，在健康的基础和纯粹的商业原则之上统一成强大的组织”。

On Friday, August 18th, the Tairiku Shimpo,
local Japanese language daily, carried a notice, of
which the attached is a translation, referring to the
impending appearance of a Russian language weekly
Nedelia.

This publication was actually registered
with the Police on May 9, 1939 (Certificate F. 67)
but would apparently have failed to appear.

Rumour has it that its impending appearance
is only possible owing to certain subsidies.

As M.A. Galkin of 25 Route Tenant de la Tour
is Russian, may I respectfully request that this matter
be handed to a Russian member of the Branch for enquiries.

Ew Golder

REPORT    Date May 9, 19 38
Subject "Nedelia" ( The Week ), Russian weekly newspaper - registration.
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

According to Mr. M.A. GALKIN, publisher and
editor of the proposed Russian illustrated weekly news-
paper entitled "NEDELIA" ( The Week ), this publication
is intended to be a purely commercial enterprise devoid
of any political significance. It will be devoted main-
ly to the life of Russian emigrants generally and to
Russian emigrants affairs in Shanghai , in particular.

Mihail Avtonomovich GALKIN, Russian, was born
on November 21, 1904 at Tomsk, Siberia. Following his gra-
duation from a middle school in Tomsk in 1919 he is re-
ported to have served in Admiral Kolchak's army in Sibe-
ria in 1919-1920 and subsequently in the Russian "White"
army in Vladivostok( 1921-1922 ).

From 1922 to 1938 he resided in Harbin where,
according to his own statement, he worked as a reporter
in various local newspapers including the "RUPOR" ( 1928-
1932 ) and the "Harbin Times" ( 1932 -1938 ). He arrived
in Shanghai from Harbin in June, 1938 and has since been
on the staff of the local Russian newspaper "SLOVO", 238
Avenue du Roi Albert.

Information to hand indicates that Galkin be-
longs to the pro-Japanese group of Russian emigrants.
A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

米哈伊尔·阿夫托诺莫维奇·加尔金（Mihail Avtonomovich GALKIN），俄罗斯人，1904年11月21日出生于西伯利亚托木斯克。据报道，他于1919年从托木斯克的一所中学毕业后，于1919-1920年间在高尔察克海军上将的西伯利亚军队中服役，随后在符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）的俄罗斯“白”军服役（1921-1922）。

1922年至1938年，他居住在哈尔滨，据他自己陈述，他在当地多家报纸担任记者，包括《RUPOR》（1928-1932）和《哈尔滨时报》（1932-1938）。他于1938年6月从哈尔滨抵达上海，此后一直在当地俄文报纸《SLOVO》任职，地址为阿尔贝王路238号。

现有资料显示，加尔金属于亲日派的俄罗斯移民群体。

Sir, 


As publisher and editor of the daily newspaper "Gelbe Post" (17, Canton Rd.), 
duly registered with the S.m.P. under the number 1-62, and as a ratepayer of the In- 
ternational Settlement, I beg to draw your attention to the following: 


today, on monday, April 6, in the forenoon, there appeared in the part of 
Shanghai lying north of Soochow Ureek several persons dressed in black, apparently of 
the Japanese nationality, and visited a number of shops in which copies of "Gelbe Post" 
were displayed for sale. They energetically demanded that the shop owners should hand 
over to them all the issues of the above named paper, such demand being granted in all 
instances. 


The shop owners tried to question these persons as to 
1) their identity, 

2) on whose behalf they were acting and 

3) the reason for their doings, 


but not a single of the above questions was answered and also 
4) no receipts were issued against the delivery of the paper. 


Furthermore, I was informed by several street sellers that they were held up 
by persons in Japanese uniforms and that all issues of the "Gelbe Post" which they had 
on hand were taken away without stating any reasons and without any receipts. 


I have been waiting that in the course of the day some information would be 
forthcoming to me, or to the office of the "Gelbe Post", 17, Canton Road, which would 
help me to clarify this entirely mysterious and unreasonable seizure of my newspaper, 
but up to this moment, viz., 5 pem.e no such information is to hand, and I am not sure 
that tomorrow's issues will not suffer the same fate. pL 


I feel compelled to bring the above occurrences to the knowledge of the S.u.P. 
and reserve my rights to claim damages suffered on account of the above. 


I remain, Sir,

rival publications.

views singly and jointly with the proprietors of the two 
papers and I must confess that the task was not a pleasant 
one. H 


|

the feude would have meant the suspension of both papers 
with the resultant loss of work for about 250 Emigrants 
or more, who were earning their living in connection with 
the two publications. 


The taking over of the "Gelbe-PUSt" was, therfore, 
a@ happy solution which entailed certain immediate sacri- 
fices for the owner of the "Shanghai Jewish Chronicle", 
but which he hopes to recoup gradually in the course of 
time. 


Hardly has, however, this happy solution been 
brought about, when it is reported to me that application 
has been made to you for the licensing of a new Emigrant 
Ger language paper. This enterprise is, I am told, to 
be financed by the English wife of a Germen Emigrant and 
amongst others a Mr. Horst Lewin and a Mr. Wolff are in- 
terested for personal reasons, to get the paper started 
a make out of it what they can whilst the going is 
good.

of the opinion that there is no justification for the a 
lication of such a paper as it would, by no means, fil 
@ public need or even an Emigrant need. The two gta 
now published, one in the morning and the other the 
evening, are ample for all purposes and a new competitor 
would only mean a new paper war, doing no one any 
and a lot of harm possibly to many.

policy was to be one “agin’' the government" i.e. black=

according to Mr. M.A. GALKIN,publisher and 

editor of the proposed Russian illustrated weekly news- 
paper entitled "NEDELIA" ( The Week ),this publication 
is intended to be a purely co:mercial enterprise devoid 
of any political significance. It will be devoted main- 
ly to the life of Russian emigrants generally and to 
Russian emigrants affairs in Shanghai ,in particular. 

Mihail Avtonomovich GALKDIN, Russian, was born 
on November 21,1904 at Somsk,Siberia. Following his gra- 
duation from a middle school in Tomsk in 1919 he is re- 
ported to have served in admiral Kolchak's army in Sibe- 
ria in 1919-1920 and subsequently in the Russian "White" 
army in Vladivostok( 1921-1922 ), 

From 1922 to 1938 he resided in Harbin where, 


according to his own statement, he worked as a reporter 


ere 


in various local newspapers including the “RUPOR" ( 1928- 
1932 ) and the “Harbin Times" ( 1932 -1938 ). He arrived 
in Shanghai from “arbin in June,1938 and has since been 
on the staff of the local Russian newspaper "SLOVO", 238 
Avenue du Roi Albert. 

Information to hand indicates that Galkin be- 


| longs to the pro-Japanese group of Russian emigrants.
